items.title: Device Mgt System won’t expose users’ data – NCC
items.description: By Prince Osuagwu The Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, has allayed fears that its new Device Management System, DMS, designed to strengthen Type Approval compliance for mobile devices in Nigeria, could give the regulator access to users’ personal data and communications. The Commission, in a statement by its Director, Corporate Affairs, Nnenna Ukoha, maintained that the insinuation was unfounded, stressing that the platform was designed solely for device identification and regulatory compliance. The clarification followed concerns over the Commission’s plan to electronically determine the Type Approval compliance of SIM-enabled devices through the DMS, which is being deployed to improve oversight of the country’s communications device ecosystem. According to the NCC, the system will maintain device identification information, including the International Mobile Equipment Identity, IMEI, numbers of devices operating in Nigeria, but will not provide access to the contents of users’ devices or personal communications. The Commission said the initiative is part of efforts to ensure that communications devices imported, sold and used in Nigeria meet applicable technical and regulatory standards. Under Section 132(2) of the Nigerian Communications Act 2003, licensed service and facilities providers, equipment manufacturers and suppliers are required to obtain Type Approval from the Commission before communications equipment can be sold or used in Nigeria. The NCC said the Device Management System would also help identify non-compliant and illegally imported devices, improve network performance and strengthen consumer confidence in devices sold in the country. It added that stolen devices reported through the appropriate channels could also be identified and blocked from operating across Nigerian mobile networks. The Commission has commenced the first phase of implementing the automated Type Approval compliance framework, working with the Nigeria Customs Service, Original Equipment Manufacturers, OEMs, importers and relevant market associations. The first phase is focused on onboarding existing devices currently held in stock and ensuring that devices imported into Nigeria going forward are appropriately registered and authenticated. NCC’s Director of Technical Standards and Network Integrity, Engr. Edoyemi Ogoh, said the Type Approval Business Rules issued in August 2024 provided the regulatory framework for establishing a Central Equipment Identity Register, CEIR, which maintains a registry of SIM-enabled communications devices in Nigeria. He said the central registry of IMEI numbers would enable the Commission to ensure that devices imported into, sold and used in Nigeria comply with applicable standards. “With the deployment of this system, all SIM-enabled communications devices brought into the country must be registered before they are sold. Devices that are not duly registered will not be permitted to operate on Nigerian networks,” Ogoh said. He added that the system would make it easier to identify illegally imported and non-compliant devices, while stolen devices could be blocked from use across Nigerian mobile networks. The NCC stressed that the DMS is therefore a regulatory and device-identification tool, rather than a platform for accessing or monitoring users’ personal communications. Vanguard News The post Device Mgt System won’t expose users’ data – NCC appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: SSNIT honours 16 stakeholders at 2025 Awards
items.description: The Social Security and National Insurance Trust (SSNIT) has honoured 16 outstanding stakeholders for their commitment and contribution to the Social Security Scheme. The recognition took place at the 2025 SSNIT Stakeholder Awards, held last month at the La Palm Royal Beach Hotel in Accra. The awardees included employers, self-employed contributors, pensioners and partner organisations. Established in 2019, the SSNIT Stakeholder Awards Scheme recognises stakeholders whose compliance, consistency and partnership have contributed to the sustainability and growth of the Social Security Scheme. Speaking at the ceremony, the Deputy Director-General of SSNIT, in charge of Operations and Benefits, Mr. Adam Sulley, reaffirmed the Trust’s efforts to creating greater value for members through innovation and improved service delivery. “We remain committed to our members by making our services more accessible, responsive and convenient,” Mr. Sulley said. Deputy Director-General of SSNIT – Operations and Benefits – Adam Sulley He highlighted recent initiatives by the Trust, including the Virtual Branch, Membership Value Programme (MVP), Co-location with partner banks and the Telehealth Service, which are aimed at improving access to SSNIT services and enhancing the experience of members. He added that the Trust was strengthening its service-led approach and leveraging data to improve its operations and service delivery. The General Manager, Operations, Philip Kofi Senyah, described the awards as an opportunity to recognise stakeholders whose contributions continued to strengthen the Social Security Scheme. He stressed that the sustainability of the Scheme depended on the collective commitment and continued collaboration of all stakeholders. Awards Among the individual awardees, Snaider Konadu Owusu received the Youngest Ambassador Award, while Elvis Agyemeng was honoured with the Loyal Contributor Award. Fidelia Aku Amevuvor received the Distinguished Service Award, while Nem Robert Kweku was recognised with the Trailblazer Self-Employed Pensioner Award. The Lifetime Dedication Award was presented to Amadu Wala, the oldest living SSNIT pensioner, while the National Pensioners’ Association (NPA) received the Outstanding Growth Partner Award. In the establishment category, Zijin Golden Ridge Limited received the Ambassador of the Trust Award. The Diamond Compliance Award was presented to Burkina Chamber of Commerce Ghana Agency, Flexi-Space Ltd and Ernest Chemists Ltd in the small, medium and large establishment categories, respectively. Scanship Ghana Limited, Hull Blyth (Ghana) Limited and The Church of Pentecost received the Excellence in Contribution Award, while Rinacand Company Limited, Bishop Bowers School and SIC Insurance Company Ltd were honoured with the Legacy Partnership Award. Speaking on behalf of the award recipients, Rev. Sis Matilda Quist of Bishop Bowers School expressed appreciation to SSNIT for the recognition. She acknowledged the importance of the collective efforts of stakeholders in supporting and strengthening the Social Security Scheme. In her closing remarks, the Ag. Member and Client Services Manager of SSNIT, Racheal Joel-Pappoe, congratulated the awardees and expressed appreciation to them for their continued support.

items.title: Police arrest man over mother’s murder in Osun
items.description: By Shina Abubakar The Osun State Police command on Wednesday disclosed that it arrested one Taye Kasali for allegedly killing his mother, Mrs Kudirat Kasali over farm dispute. A statement issued by the command’s Public Relations Officer DSP Abiodun Ojelabi disclosed that the police in Bode-Osi in Ola-Oluwa local government received report that the deceased and her son were missing on September 1, 2026. Following the report, operatives from the command embarked on investigation and intelligence led to the arrest of the son, Taye, on September 7, 2026, and later confessed to killing his mother. The suspect led the police team to the farm where the body of his mother was recovered from a shallow grave along with the matchet used to slit the deceased’s throat before burying her. The statement disclosed that his mother had been referring to him as a mad person and threatening to lease out the farmland which the suspect claimed is the family’s source of income. Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police Ibrahim Zungura has directed thorough investigation into the incident with view to charging him to court to face the wrath of he law. He also assured the residents of the State that Justice will be served in the case, urging the public to always report the cases of missing persons promptly to police as well s other criminal activities in their communities. The post Police arrest man over mother’s murder in Osun appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Obi: Ortom condemns blockade, says Alia is responsible
items.description: By Dickson Omobola Former Governor Samuel Ortom of Benue State has condemned the blockade of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, from visiting Yelwata community in Guma Local Government Area of the state, accusing Governor Hyacinth Alia of disrespecting the rule of law. Ortom said the incident was a reflection of the situation in Benue, noting that it was unfortunate that a clergyman who should be telling the truth was telling lies. Speaking on Politics Today, a Channels Television programme, Wednesday, Ortom alleged that Alia was behind the incident and challenged the governor to swear by the Bible that he was not aware of what happened. His words: “In Benue State, we have a government that does not believe in the rule of law. We have a government in Benue State that is out for lawlessness. We begin to wonder, if all of us will not respect the rule of law, but also join him in ensuring lawlessness, where are we going to be? This is a supposed man of God, a supposed priest of the Catholic Church. We know that even in the scriptures that we lean on, it says that we must respect the laws of the land. “But unfortunately, we have somebody who says he’s a Catholic priest and does not respect the rule of law in any way. I condemn what happened yesterday. It is wrong not to allow Peter Obi to visit Benue and sympathise with those people whose people were killed. It was wrong, and that is the kind of government that we have in Benue State today. “Governor Alia has been doing it. Governor Alia was one person who said, ‘No Alia, no Benue,’ and went to remove a Chief Judge through these thugs. Alia sent tippers with loads of sand to block the Chief Judge’s office. He has been saying that if nobody accepts him, he will not accept any other person. “I say that it is unfortunate that somebody who is supposed to be a reverend father is telling lies. Can he come out and swear by the Bible that he claims to be a reverend priest and say that he was not aware of what happened yesterday? It was a deliberate attempt. He did it. Ask any other person. “Alia himself, the governor of Benue State, is involved in this matter. He cannot deny that. I am not supporting Peter Obi. But it is wrong.” Meanwhile, former Governor of Bayelsa State and national leader of the NDC, Seriake Dickson, called for a thorough investigation and prosecution of those involved, saying Nigerians deserve to know the extent of complicity. Speaking on Newsnight, an Arise TV programme, Wednesday, he said there had been allegations that some government officials were involved in the incident and urged the authorities to establish whether the allegations were true. His words: “This happening, while campaigns have officially started, sends a very dangerous signal, and the point has to be made clearly that this is not only condemnable, it is criminal. This is rascality of the highest order, and this is intolerable. There has to be punishment for this, so that we can say, well, however bad things may have gone in this country, we can’t accept this to go on. Otherwise, we may have a situation where candidates will be attacked everywhere, or people will be encouraged wrongly to think or assume that a presidential candidate, or even any other candidate or any other Nigerian, needs a visa of some kind to be able to participate in any activity he or she wants to, or to visit any state. “No Nigerian citizen, by our Constitution and our laws, needs anyone’s permission or approval to visit a state. More so, when we are dealing with a presidential candidate, a high-profile personality, at a period of political campaigns, you stop the man with thugs. No, that is not encouraging. It sounds almost obscene. It tells where we have gone as a country, but we must speak against it. “We have just listened to the remarks that the Commissioner of Police made, even though we were all concerned about what steps the police took at that venue, or to prevent it. One of the first things I asked when it occurred, I called the national chairman and asked, was there notification to the state authorities? And they brought a copy of a letter, a letter by the state chairman to the Commissioner of Police. “Once you have informed the Commissioner of Police about the visit or activities of a politician or a high-profile personality, that is to be treated as information to the state authorities because the Commissioner of Police is the chief law enforcement officer of every state. “I’m pleased with the steps they have taken. I’m not surprised, but steps should have been taken to prevent it. By tomorrow, there will be a formal petition from our party to the Inspector-General and then to the Attorney-General of the Federation. And I think we have gotten to a point, before campaigns really kick off, for even the President of the country to weigh in on this. “He is sitting at the apex of the political system, and he’s not just President of the APC, he’s not just President of a particular set of people. He is the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, and his job is not to talk about economic policies, which we disagree with. His job is not just political stability and security matters, which they are not doing well either. But part of the duties and responsibilities of the President in our system includes the preservation and protection of the democratic order and the democratic system.” The post Obi: Ortom condemns blockade, says Alia is responsible appeared first on Vanguard News .

Naa Shika Adu presents Vernacular of Play: An art exhibition inspired by sport, identity and social impact
items.description: Former women’s professional tennis player and internationally certified tennis coach Naa Shika Adu is set to launch Vernacular of Play on 11 September 2026, a compelling multidisciplinary art exhibition exploring the connections between movement, language and cultural expression in sport and everyday life. The exhibition is supported by the Edward Osei Boakye Trust and features a creative collaboration with artist Reginald Kofi Boateng, bringing together sport and visual art in a thought-provoking exploration of play, identity and culture. The exhibition reinterprets tennis as more than a competitive activity, positioning it as a powerful tool for social commentary. At its core, Vernacular of Play explores how movement transcends words, and how play serves as a compelling mirror of society, capturing its rhythms, inequalities, aspirations, and moments of collective joy. Central to this concept is the term “vernacular,” which historically carried negative connotations within colonial educational systems where indigenous speech and identity were often suppressed. In this context, the term is reclaimed and transformed into a symbol of cultural identity, memory and expression. Inspired by her experiences as both an athlete and a youth development advocate, Naa Shika creates an immersive space where art and sport intersect. Through a carefully assembled collection of works curated by Whitney Chinonye Ernest, the exhibition highlights themes of resilience, aspiration, discipline and community, while celebrating the universal significance of play. According to Naa Shika, “the body speaks long before words are formed. In Vernacular of Play, every movement, a serve, a sprint, a pause, or a moment of stillness becomes a sentence in a larger story, expressing emotions, struggles and triumphs that transcend language.” The exhibition further challenges the perception of sport as neutral. Tennis, often linked to privilege and exclusivity, is reframed through African perspectives and lived experiences. By combining performance, visual art, sound, archival storytelling and embodied movement, the project explores the deeper social meanings embedded within the choreography of play and how history is carried within the body, even in competitive spaces. Beyond its artistic intent, the exhibition also serves a broader social purpose. It supports the Africa Sports Alliance (ASA) Foundation, founded by Naa Shika, which is dedicated to using sport as a vehicle for youth empowerment across Africa. Through mentorship, structured programmes and access to opportunities, the Foundation seeks to develop talent, create employment pathways and equip young people with essential life skills. Vernacular of Play is therefore positioned as both a cultural and social engagement platform, bringing together artists, athletes, educators, corporate partners and the wider community in support of youth development. Its impact lies in its ability to connect sport, art and social consciousness in a way that is inclusive, participatory and culturally relevant. The exhibition creates opportunities for African youth to see themselves represented within contemporary narratives, while encouraging dialogue on issues such as access to sport, representation, postcolonial identity and cultural preservation. Ultimately, Vernacular of Play invites audiences to move beyond observation to active engagement, reflecting on how movement, language and play influence how societies remember the past, respond to the present and shape the future. It stands as a powerful testament to Naa Shika Adu’s commitment to driving meaningful change beyond the tennis court.

items.title: Camps de Tindouf : le Maroc appelle le HCR à financer des solutions durables
items.description: Devant le Comité permanent du HCR, le Maroc a dénoncé un système de financement des camps de Tindouf qui, depuis des décennies, entretient la crise au lieu de la résoudre, et appelé l'organisation à faire des « solutions durables » une priorité de sa planification budgétaire. Face à des besoins qui progressent et un budget qui impose des arbitrages douloureux, le Maroc a appelé, mercredi à Genève, le Haut-Commissariat des Nations unies pour les réfugiés (HCR) à inscrire les “solutions durables” dans sa planification budgétaire pour les camps de Tindouf, en Algérie, estimant que les financements consacrés depuis plusieurs décennies à cette situation reconduisent un “régime de maintien coûteux” plutôt qu’ils ne contribuent à la résoudre. Ces solutions durables consistent en le retour dans la dignité des populations concernées, conformément à l'appel solennel du Roi Mohammed VI, la réinstallation dans des pays tiers disposés à y contribuer et l'intégration dans le pays d'accueil, a indiqué l’ambassadeur représentant permanent du Maroc auprès de l’ONU et des autres organisations internationales à Genève, Omar Zniber, lors des travaux du Comité permanent du HCR. “Depuis 2021, près de 90 millions de dollars ont été mobilisés par le HCR dans les camps de Tindouf, en Algérie. Et dans le même temps, année après année, tout a régressé : le taux de malnutrition a doublé, l'autonomie économique s'est effacée, et l'accès à l’emploi demeure interdit – de sorte que la dépense a crû quand l'espérance, elle, a décru” , a-t-il relevé. Selon Omar Zniber, ces chiffres “ne décrivent pas un programme de protection” mais “un régime de maintien” , coûteux dans un contexte budgétaire contraint et insuffisant au regard des besoins des personnes concernées. A cet égard, l’ambassadeur a rappelé que le droit international des réfugiés prévoit “trois solutions durables” , à savoir “ le rapatriement librement consenti, la réinstallation et l’intégration dans le pays d’accueil ”, estimant que ce sont ces solutions qui permettent de mettre fin à la prolongation des dépenses liées aux situations de déplacement prolongé. Il a par ailleurs affirmé que le Royaume “assume pleinement sa part de cette responsabilité”, soulignant que cet engagement s'inscrit désormais dans “un cadre transformé: en adoptant la résolution 2797, le Conseil de sécurité a consacré l'initiative marocaine d’autonomie ouvrant un horizon politique là où ne subsistait qu'un statu quo”. A ce titre, “l'appel solennel du Roi Mohammed VI, au retour dans la dignité des populations concernées vaut engagement d'accueil, sans condition et sur une base strictement individuelle et volontaire” , a-t-il ajouté, notant que le Maroc “soutient également, avec la même conviction, les deux autres solutions – la réinstallation dans des pays tiers disposés à y contribuer et l'intégration dans le pays d'accueil – selon le choix libre de chaque personne”. Cette approche n'est pas isolée, a-t-il soutenu, expliquant qu’un nombre important d'États donateurs, parmi les premiers contributeurs au budget, se déclarent “prêts à financer ce qui résout plutôt que ce qui perdure”. Omar Zniber a, de ce fait, invité le HCR à “saisir cette disponibilité, en inscrivant les solutions durables au cœur de sa planification budgétaire et en engageant, avec les États concernés et les partenaires volontaires, l'examen des trois solutions avant la session du Comité exécutif”. “L’objectif de réduire de moitié les situations prolongées d’ici 2035 est d’abord un objectif budgétaire: il ne se décidera pas ailleurs qu'ici, dans l'affectation de chaque dollar ”, a-t-il conclu. items.title: Ghana wastes up to 50% of fruits and vegetables annually – Agrofresh
items.description: Ghana wastes between 40% and 50% of its fruits and vegetables annually, social entrepreneur, innovator and changemaker Mathias Charles Yabe has said. He said the losses occur across the food value chain, from farms and marketplaces to homes, restaurants and food joints. Speaking on the 13th edition of the Loud and Green X-Space on JoyNews, Mr Yabe said the scale of food waste remained a major challenge requiring practical interventions. “Just in Ghana, we see at least about 40% of our food is being wasted in terms of fruits and vegetables being wasted every year. About 40 to 50%. So that is a current situation in Ghana,” he said. Mr Yabe said his interest in addressing post-harvest losses was influenced by experiences in farming communities, including a case where a farmer’s tomatoes were left to rot because buyers failed to arrive on time and there was no facility to store the produce. He said the challenge was particularly acute in farming communities without reliable access to electricity, where conventional refrigeration systems can be difficult to deploy. His company, Agrofresh, has consequently developed solar-powered refrigeration systems designed for farms and communities. “Basically, we are building fridges on farms and in communities. Essentially, these fridges are supposed to help preserve food and extend its shelf life, especially fruits and vegetables, from five days to up to 21 days,” he said. Mr Yabe said the refrigerators are powered by solar energy and are intended to serve communities that are off the national electricity grid. Agrofresh has also introduced solar-powered refrigerated tricycles to help reduce losses during the transportation of fresh produce. “We recently introduced solar-powered refrigerator tricycles. These tricycles are a complementary solution to the stationary and then the mobile refrigerated units,” he said. According to Mr Yabe, the intervention gives farmers another option for preserving their produce while it is being transported to markets. He said reducing post-harvest losses could simultaneously improve farmers’ incomes, strengthen food supply and reduce the environmental impact of food waste. The discussion formed part of the 13th edition of the Loud and Green X-Space, which examined opportunities emerging from Ghana’s climate challenges.

items.title: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra vs iPhone Duo: Which foldable phone is better?
items.description: The Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra and Apple iPhone Duo are now competing for the attention of consumers looking for a premium foldable smartphone, with both devices offering large displays, powerful processors and high-end features. Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra and Apple’s first foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo, take different approaches to the foldable phone experience. While Samsung has several years of experience making foldable smartphones, Apple is entering the market with a device designed to combine the iPhone experience with a larger, tablet-like display. Here’s how the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra compares with the iPhone Duo. Display The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra has a larger 8-inch internal AMOLED display and a 6.5-inch cover screen. The iPhone Duo features a 7.6-inch internal OLED display and a smaller 5.4-inch external display. Samsung therefore has the advantage for users who want as much screen space as possible when the phone is unfolded. The larger display is particularly useful for browsing, watching videos, editing documents and running multiple applications simultaneously. Performance The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy processor. Apple’s iPhone Duo runs on the company’s latest A20 Pro chip. Both processors are designed for demanding applications, gaming and artificial intelligence features. However, direct performance comparisons will require independent benchmark and real-world testing before a clear winner can be declared. Camera Samsung has the more versatile camera setup. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra features a 200MP main camera, a 50MP ultrawide camera and a 10MP telephoto camera with 3x optical zoom. The iPhone Duo, meanwhile, uses two 48MP rear cameras. Although camera quality cannot be judged by megapixel counts alone, Samsung’s dedicated telephoto camera gives the Fold 8 Ultra an advantage for users who regularly photograph distant subjects. Apple, however, has a long-standing reputation for computational photography and video recording, meaning the iPhone Duo could still compete strongly despite having fewer cameras. Battery Samsung equips the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra with a 5,000mAh battery. Apple uses a dual-cell battery design in the iPhone Duo and has focused on delivering all-day battery life despite the phone’s thin foldable design. On paper, Samsung has the advantage in battery capacity, but actual battery performance will depend on factors including software optimisation, display usage and processor efficiency. Multitasking and productivity This is one area where the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra has a major advantage. Samsung has spent years developing its foldable software, allowing users to run multiple applications on the large internal display. The Fold 8 Ultra can effectively function as a small tablet when unfolded, making it particularly useful for people who work from their phones. Apple has also introduced software features designed specifically for the larger display of the iPhone Duo, but Samsung’s experience gives it an advantage in foldable multitasking. Durability The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra has an IP48 rating. The iPhone Duo has a higher IP68 rating, giving Apple’s device an advantage in water and dust resistance. Durability remains an important consideration for foldable phones because their flexible displays and hinges are more complicated than those found on conventional smartphones. Price The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra starts at around $2,100, while Apple’s iPhone Duo starts at $1,999. That makes Apple’s first foldable iPhone slightly cheaper at launch. However, prices in markets such as Nigeria can differ considerably from US launch prices because of taxes, import costs, exchange rates and retailer margins. Which one should you buy? The Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra is the stronger choice for users who prioritise productivity, multitasking, camera versatility and a large internal display. Samsung’s experience in the foldable market also means buyers are getting a more mature foldable platform. The iPhone Duo, on the other hand, is likely to appeal most to existing Apple users who want a foldable phone without leaving the iOS ecosystem. For users with a MacBook, Apple Watch, AirPods and other Apple devices, the iPhone Duo offers the convenience of keeping everything within Apple’s ecosystem. Vanguard News The post Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra vs iPhone Duo: Which foldable phone is better? appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Travelers Face More Flight Delays After Major Air Traffic Disruption at UK Airports
All the Places Trump Was on 9/11
items.description: W here were you on 9/11? Every American old enough to remember the day has an answer to that question. President Trump has several. At a ceremony honoring first responders and victims’ families yesterday, Trump offered an elaborate account of where he was in the hours and days after nearly 3,000 Americans were killed. “I was building a big building in New York, and I took the whole crew down there right after this happened, and they had no hesitation; everybody went down with me. We went down as a big group of people. Wasn’t too much we could do, I’ll be honest. It was raw—nobody had seen anything like it, ever.” The story presents significant problems in terms of its relationship to reality. Listeners could be forgiven for interpreting Trump’s remarks as a reference to his whereabouts on the day of the attack itself. (The president clarified that timeline last night: “I was there, obviously not on the same day as the collapse, but shortly thereafter, with a large group of Construction Workers,” he wrote in a Truth Social post.) It is true that two days after the attack, on September 13, Trump was interviewed by reporters while walking in Lower Manhattan. The president has previously made variations of the same claim—that he and the employees he sent downtown helped clear rubble in the days following the attack. “Everyone who helped clear the rubble—and I was there, and I watched, and I helped a little bit” was his version of it on the 2016 campaign trail. But supporting evidence is scant, and the whole account is likely an exaggeration. Richard Alles, a retired New York City Fire Department deputy chief who had a supervisory role in the efforts, said in 2019 not only that he never witnessed Trump at the site, but that the account doesn’t add up: “He was a private citizen at the time. I don’t know what kind of role he could have possibly played.” And, Alles added , if Trump had indeed sent workers, as he has claimed, there would be a record of it: “Is there a chance he was ever down there by himself and I didn’t know it? It’s possible, but I know of no one who ever witnessed him there.” Nevertheless, Trump pressed on, veering into territory even further detached from verifiable fact. The U.S. Steel Building—a skyscraper in Lower Manhattan known today as One Liberty Plaza—was “really creaking,” Trump said at yesterday’s ceremony. “I’ll never forget: two firemen. We thought it was coming down on top of us and two firemen—big, strong guys. And I’m not the smallest guy in the world. They grabbed me under the arms, said, ‘Gotta get outta here.’ And they literally lifted me up—this is not easy to do; I’m big. They lifted me up, and they started running with me. I said, ‘Fellas, I can run myself.’ But they were amazing, but they thought it was coming down. It didn’t come down: U.S. Steel.” There was, in fact, public concern in the days following the attack that the building at One Liberty Plaza could collapse. But the notion that Trump was inside the building and rushed out by firefighters has not been corroborated by any evidence. The president has offered versions of the same account before, though in less colorful form. In 2016, he told a story about being evacuated by firefighters—but in that rendition, it took place “a couple of days” after the collapse, and the U.S. Steel building was “not so far from us” when the two “massive guys” grabbed him. “I never knew I could run that fast,” he said then. In 2021, Trump likewise recalled two firemen grabbing him after hearing “creaks.” Trump’s whereabouts on September 11 are no mystery. They are fairly well documented by his own prior statements about watching the attacks unfold from his home in Trump Tower, about four miles north of the Twin Towers. For those who have reason to doubt Trump’s statements, his whereabouts are also documented on video. “I have a window that looks directly at the World Trade Center, and I saw this huge explosion,” he said in a phone interview with a New Jersey news channel on 9/11. “For years, I’ve looked right directly at the building—I’d see the Empire State Building in the foreground and the World Trade Center in the background—and now I’m looking at absolutely nothing. It’s just gone, and it’s just hard to believe.” Trump’s view may have been clear, but his recollection of September 11 has been murky, as reporters have tracked for more than a decade. Sometimes, in his accounts, he watched the second plane hit the World Trade Center from his apartment in Trump Tower; when he called into the live broadcast that day, he did not mention having witnessed the second jet. Sometimes, he claims to have personally seen people jumping from the Twin Towers. “I have a window in my apartment that specifically was aimed at the World Trade Center,” he said in 2015 on the campaign trail, “and I watched as people jumped.” In his TV interview the day of the attack, he didn’t see those scenes himself but talked to someone who had. “I have somebody that was down there who witnessed at least 10 people jumping out of the building from 70 and 80 stories up in the air,” Trump said. The president has also embellished what he saw in news coverage on that day, most notoriously claiming to have seen widespread celebrations by Muslim residents in New Jersey. “I watched when the World Trade Center came tumbling down,” he said in a 2015 stump speech. “And I watched in Jersey City, New Jersey, where thousands and thousands of people were cheering as that building was coming down.” That claim has been thoroughly disproved. A professor who spent months combing through news reels and video archives from that day found one possible instance that could slightly resemble those events—a few Arab American teenagers who briefly gathered in front of a library in South Paterson in a way that could be seen as celebratory. Even the live phone interview Trump participated in on the day of the attack contains inaccuracies. On the call, Trump said that one of his buildings was now the tallest in downtown Manhattan: “Forty Wall Street actually was the second-tallest building in downtown Manhattan,” he said when asked whether his property had been damaged. “When they built the World Trade Center, it became known as the second tallest. And now it’s the tallest.” But as The Washington Post documented , using data from the Council on Tall Buildings and Urban Habitat, neither claim was true. Forty Wall Street was the tallest building for only about two years and that was in the 1930s, before Trump was born. A t the center of yesterday’s ceremony was an important honor—one that Trump had promised to bestow months prior. Welles Crowther, who was first identified as “the man in the red bandana” in a 2002 New York Times story, rescued more than a dozen people from the South Tower before being killed when the building collapsed. His parents, who had given him a red bandana as a boy and knew that he always carried it with him, were able to recognize him by that detail and confirmed through the survivors that their son had helped them. Crowther was an equities trader and a volunteer firefighter, and he was 24 years old when he died. While posthumously awarding the Presidential Medal of Freedom to Crowther, Trump drew the focus to himself, comparing his own fame to that of the fallen hero: “The Man in the Red Bandana, he’s become more famous than me—I don’t like it. Very unhappy. But he’s become much more famous than me.” [ Read: Trump is putting his face on everything ] When the president has brought up 9/11 lately, the remark has usually been severed from the attack, its victims, or its perpetrators. This year, Trump has tended to mention the day in the context of lambasting political opponents. He’s invoked it on several recent occasions—alongside World War I, World War II, and Pearl Harbor—when arguing that the attack and all three of those historical calamities are dwarfed by the danger communism poses to America today. Critics have noted that other presidents, both Republican and Democrat, might have faced months of blowback—if not the end of their political careers—were they caught exaggerating or outright inventing aspects of their experience on one of the most catastrophic days in American history. But Trump has rarely if ever paid a real political price for misleading statements. In a second term marked by his fixation on his legacy, Trump’s relationship with history has often involved “taking bits and pieces from a grab bag and turning it into a story that’s useful to him—either politically useful, as in the case of his fabrication about Muslims celebrating 9/11, or making himself the center of a story that obviously he was not the center of 25 years ago,” Tim Naftali, a presidential historian at Columbia’s School of International and Public Affairs, told me. The fabrications are unlikely to stop, he said, especially as the president ages . “It doesn’t happen the same to all men in their 80s, but we may see more of this: new recollections about the past that we’ve never heard before, because they never happened,” Naftali said. The White House did not address my specific questions about the president’s most recent claims, but Davis Ingle, a White House spokesperson, said in a statement that the president “was relaying his experience of a city reeling” from the attacks. September 11 continues to be a point of tension about what the government owed, and continues to owe, those who were most affected. The mayor’s office released more than 170,000 pages of city records this week showing that city officials misled New Yorkers about air quality following the attacks. And the health toll continues to grow; the number of 9/11 survivors receiving assistance for cancer treatment roughly tripled over the past five years, according to a Washington Post analysis of reports by the World Trade Center Health Program, which funds health care for responders and survivors. Twenty-five years later, Americans everywhere will pause to remember what the nation lost that day—both those who suffered directly and those who lived through it by watching the tragedy unfold from the safety of their homes, much as Trump did.

items.title: Village gastronomique de Paris : ce qui vous attend au pavillon Algérie
items.description: Parmi les 73 pays qui vont participer à la 10e édition du Village international de la gastronomie de Paris, du 10 au 13 septembre, figure l’Algérie, qui s’est taillé une part du lion concernant le nombre des stands. Cet évènement international verra la participation de chefs cuisiniers venus des quatre coins du monde, dont Na Nora, qui va préparer sa célèbre galette farcie et un couscous spécial. Les Algériens ne seront pas en reste, et tenteront de hisser le drapeau national au plus haut, grâce notamment à la richesse de sa cuisine et à l’authenticité de ses produits de terroir. La nouvelle édition de cet événement sera donc lancée demain, jeudi 10 septembre. Le Village international de la gastronomie s’installera Place de la Concorde, à deux pas des Champs-Elysées. Les visiteurs auront donc l’occasion de déguster des préparations culinaires en tout genre, notamment algériennes, pas loin de la Tour Eiffel. Village gastronomique de Paris : le pavillon algérien s’élargit Lors de cet évènement, l’Algérie aura droit à deux stands, de 9 m² chacun, en ce qui concerne la gastronomie, et quatre autres stands pour ce qui est des produits du terroir, a dévoilé Makhlouf Chalal, organisateur du stand Algérie, à VVA , samedi dernier. L’Algérie figure ainsi parmi les rares pays qui bénéficient d’autant de stands lors de cet évènement culinaire international. L’organisateur algérien souligne que le pavillon DZ a doublé d’espace “après le succès de l’année passée . Ce nombre de stands peut facilement s'expliquer par la richesse et la diversité de la cuisine algérienne, qui propose, entre autres, couscous, rechta, chakhchoukha, kesra, bourek. Les produits de terroir algériens sont aussi légion. On cite notamment l'huile d'olive de Kabylie, les dattes Deglet Nour, les figues sèches de Béni Maouche, ou encore les divers produits laitiers traditionnels. Pavillon algérien : plusieurs activités au menu Contacté par TSA, M. Chalal a indiqué que le pavillon DZ proposera aussi plusieurs activités, notamment un défilé de tenues traditionnelles (Kaftan, Karakou, Blouza, Robe kabyle, Chedda, etc) le 12 septembre à 10h et un spectacle assuré par une troupe folklorique, le 11 septembre à 19h. Pour ce qui est de la gastronomie, plusieurs chefs algériens seront au rendez-vous. Na Nora (Nora Sadki), la célèbre cheffe du restaurant Majouja à Paris, participera à l'événement. “Au sein du Pavillon algérien, j’aurais le plaisir de vous accueillir pour 4 jours de célébration de notre patrimoine culinaire et de tous les plats qui nous rassemblent”, a-t-elle écrit, soulignant qu’il s’agit d’une occasion “de mettre en lumière les artisans, les chefs et les producteurs locaux”. Na Nora va préparer la galette farcie ou la pizza kabyle que les visiteurs pourront déguster. « Il y aura aussi une surprise vendredi avec le couscous algérien », annonce la cheffe algérienne à TSA. « Du couscous avec du kedid (viande séchée) », précise-t-elle. Une première au Village gastronomique de Paris. La cuisine algérienne est si riche et son terroir si généreux. Les six stands qui représenteront en tout l’Algérie au sein de ce village promettent de faire découvrir aux visiteurs des délices inoubliables et un savoir-faire millénaire. L’article Village gastronomique de Paris : ce qui vous attend au pavillon Algérie est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: CSSPS deploys more personnel to ease delays at resolution centres
items.description: The Computerised School Selection and Placement System (CSSPS) has deployed additional personnel to some resolution centres across the country following concerns over long queues and delays in addressing parents’ placement challenges. Speaking on Joy FM’s Newsnight , the Media Relations Officer at the Ministry of Education, Hashmin Mohammed, said the move was prompted by reports of some centres struggling to attend to the large number of parents seeking assistance. “We have been notified of the delays and then the long queues across some of the resolution centres in the country, and accordingly the coordinator for the CSSPS, with the support of some of the ministry officials, have decided to deploy more personnel into the areas that are unable to attend to the complainants with speed of time,” he said. Mr Mohammed said the placement authorities had also established a decentralised system to make it easier for parents to have their concerns addressed. He explained that the resolution centres operate a 24-hour service, with parents issued tickets that enable them to track the progress of their complaints. He, however, acknowledged that the challenges would persist unless the gap between available vacancies and students’ preferred schools is addressed. “The problem that exists at the moment is just the disparity between where vacancies exist and then the mismatch between the choices of the students, and that is what we are currently dealing at the moment,” he said. According to him, thousands of parents have so far had their concerns addressed, although he could not provide an immediate figure. Mr Mohammed also cautioned parents against paying money to individuals to fast-track their placement concerns. He said allegations of some persons demanding money at resolution centres had been brought to the attention of officials in the Ashanti Region, who have been asked to take steps to prevent such practices. He stressed that parents are not required to pay any official or third party for CSSPS placement services.

items.title: Obi Attack: SERAP urges Tinubu to direct IGP to take over case
items.description: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has condemned the reported attack on Peter Obi, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), and his entourage in Benue State. In a statement on Wednesday signed by Kolawole Oluwadare, SERAP Deputy Director, it urged President Bola Tinubu to “direct the Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu to take over the investigation into the incident, ensure a prompt, thorough, impartial, transparent and effective investigation, and identify anyone responsible for the attack and anyone who sponsored, facilitated or otherwise aided it, with a view to prosecution where there is sufficient admissible evidence.” Obi was reportedly visiting Benue State on Tuesday when suspected thugs confronted and stopped his convoy along Gboko Road in Makurdi, near the Air Force Base. The incident reportedly occurred shortly after the convoy arrived in the state. The Benue State Police Command has confirmed the incident and commenced an investigation. The organisation said: “the IGP should take over the case to ensure that the investigation is conducted independently and comprehensively, including determining whether any public officials, political actors or other persons were involved in, sponsored, facilitated or condoned the reported attack.” SERAP said: “The reported attack is a serious threat to political participation, civic space and Nigeria’s democratic process. It is an affront to the 1999 Constitution (as amended) and Nigeria’s international human rights obligations, including under the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights, to which Nigeria is a state party.” According to SERAP, “The authorities must ensure that politicians, candidates, journalists, civil society actors and other citizens are able to freely exercise their rights to freedom of expression, peaceful assembly, association, and political participation without fear of intimidation or attack.” The statement, read, in part: “SERAP is seriously concerned that attacks, threats and intimidation against political actors undermine constitutionally and internationally guaranteed human rights and risk further shrinking Nigeria’s already fragile civic and political space, particularly as the country moves towards the 2027 general elections.” “The reported incident must also be viewed against Nigeria’s troubling history of political violence, intimidation and impunity.” “The failure to investigate and prosecute political violence would deny victims justice and create an atmosphere of impunity that emboldens further attacks.” “Allowing attacks and intimidation against political opponents to go unpunished would undermine the rule of law and public confidence in Nigeria’s democratic institutions.” “No individual or political group should be above the law. Impunity for political violence can only embolden further attacks and threaten the integrity of Nigeria’s democratic process.” “SERAP urges all political parties, candidates, supporters and public officials to refrain from threats, inflammatory rhetoric and violence and to respect the rights of political opponents and citizens to participate freely in public affairs.” “The Nigerian Constitution guarantees rights freedom of expression, peaceful assembly and association. Article 13 of the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights and Article 25 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights guarantee the right of every citizen to participate freely in the government of their country.” “These rights would be meaningless if political actors and citizens could not exercise them without fear of threats, intimidation or violence.” “Nigeria cannot afford a repetition of the cycle of political violence and impunity that has undermined previous elections. President Tinubu must act swiftly to direct the Inspector General of Police to establish the facts, identify anyone responsible and their sponsors, hold them accountable and protect political participants ahead of the 2027 general elections.” “Accountability for the reported attack is essential not only to secure justice but also to send a clear message that political violence and intimidation will not be tolerated.” The post Obi Attack: SERAP urges Tinubu to direct IGP to take over case appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Programme Génération AI & IoT : six mois après son lancement, le programme national passe à l’échelle
items.description: S’inscrivant dans la dynamique impulsée par les Hautes Orientations du Roi Mohammed VI, qui placent la jeunesse, le développement de ses compétences et son accès aux opportunités d’avenir au cœur des priorités du Royaume, le programme national Génération AIoT franchit une nouvelle étape de son déploiement. Cette initiative s’inscrit pleinement dans les ambitions de Maroc Digital 2030 et contribue à la mise en œuvre de la feuille de route « AI Made in Morocco », en misant sur le développement des compétences nationales dans les technologies de l’intelligence artificielle et de l’Internet des objets, au service de l’innovation, de l’emploi et de la souveraineté numérique du Royaume. Fruit d’un partenariat stratégique entre le Ministère de la Transition numérique et de la Réforme de l’Administration, la Fondation Mohammed V pour la Solidarité et ABA Technology, Génération AIoT ambitionne de préparer une nouvelle génération de talents marocains aux technologies qui façonnent l’économie de demain, notamment l’Intelligence Artificielle, l’Agentic AI, le Physical AI et l’IoT, en associant formation et mise en application sur des projets concrets. À l’occasion de sa visite du centre de Salé, Madame Amal El Fallah Serghouchni, Ministre déléguée auprès du Chef du Gouvernement chargée de la Transition numérique et de la Réforme de l’Administration, a constaté les premiers résultats du programme, six mois seulement après son lancement. Signé et lancé en février 2026, Génération AIoT a déjà enregistré plus de 2 118 candidatures et compte 95 talents à Salé et Casablanca. À Salé, la première promotion de 46 talents a achevé en quatre mois son cursus de formation et de spécialisation avant de passer, dès le 24 juin, aux projets en environnement professionnel. 100 % des talents entrés en phase d’immersion sont aujourd’hui intégrés à des projets appliqués, couvrant notamment la santé, les mines et l’industrie, la finance et la logistique, la recherche scientifique, l’éducation et les technologies numériques. Fort de ces premiers résultats, le programme entre désormais dans sa phase de montée en puissance nationale, avec l’ouverture de nouvelles promotions à Casablanca, Fès et Oujda, en complément de Salé. Avec 3 promotions à Casablanca, 2 à Fès et 2 à Oujda, Génération AIoT vise un régime de croisière de 1 200 talents formés par an dès février 2027. En moins d’un an, Génération AIoT entend ainsi passer du lancement à une capacité nationale de 1 200 talents par an, avec une ambition : faire de la jeunesse marocaine un acteur de la transformation technologique et productive du Royaume. The post Programme Génération AI & IoT : six mois après son lancement, le programme national passe à l’échelle appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Clôture du PASS III : le Maroc et l’UE préparent l’après-réforme sanitaire
items.description: À Rabat, la cérémonie de clôture du Programme d’appui au secteur de la santé (PASS III) a été l’occasion pour le Maroc et l’Union européenne de dresser le bilan de six années de coopération, tout en esquissant les contours d’un partenariat renouvelé autour de la souveraineté sanitaire, de la transformation numérique et du renforcement des ressources humaines. La clôture du Programme d’appui au secteur de la santé (PASS III), organisée mercredi 9 septembre à Rabat, a marqué bien davantage que la fin d’un cycle de coopération entre le Maroc et l’Union européenne. Elle a surtout servi de tribune aux deux partenaires pour affirmer leur volonté de prolonger et d’approfondir une collaboration engagée depuis plus de deux décennies dans le domaine de la santé. Signé en 2020, le PASS III a accompagné le Royaume dans plusieurs chantiers structurants : renforcement des capacités de veille et de réponse aux crises sanitaires, amélioration de la gouvernance du système de santé, développement des soins de santé primaires, démarches d’accréditation hospitalière ou encore préparation de la nouvelle gouvernance territoriale du secteur. Présent à la cérémonie, le ministre de la santé et de la protection sociale, Amine Tehraoui, a salué un programme qui « a accompagné le Maroc dans le renforcement de ses capacités de veille, de préparation et de réponse aux crises sanitaires », tout en contribuant à la modernisation de l’offre de soins et à la préparation des réformes en cours. Le ministre a également rappelé le soutien apporté par l’Union européenne à la reconstruction et à la mise à niveau des établissements de santé touchés par le séisme d’Al Haouz, soulignant que ces réalisations constituent des « acquis importants » pour le système sanitaire national. Une coopération bâtie sur les réformes Pour l’ambassadeur de l’Union européenne au Maroc, Dimiter Tzantchev, le PASS III illustre la profondeur d’une relation qui dépasse le simple cadre de l’assistance technique ou financière. « Ce programme n’est pas seulement un appui technique ou financier. Il est l’illustration d’une ambition partagée : accompagner les réformes du système de santé marocain dans une approche structurante, durable et centrée sur les besoins de la population », a-t-il déclaré. Selon le diplomate européen, les résultats du programme se mesurent autant à travers les outils de pilotage développés qu’à travers le renforcement des capacités institutionnelles et techniques des acteurs du secteur. Il a notamment mis en avant les actions de formation, les dispositifs d’accréditation hospitalière, les mécanismes de suivi ainsi que les expérimentations territoriales destinées à préparer les évolutions futures du système de santé. Dimiter Tzantchev a insisté sur le fait que « la transformation d’un système de santé ne repose pas uniquement sur des investissements matériels », mais aussi sur « des réformes de gouvernance, des outils fiables, des compétences renforcées, des mécanismes de coordination efficaces et une vision de long terme ». La santé, nouveau pilier du partenariat euro-méditerranéen Au-delà du bilan, les deux parties ont surtout mis l’accent sur les perspectives d’avenir. Pour l’ambassadeur européen, la santé est devenue un enjeu stratégique dans un contexte marqué par les transitions sanitaires, démographiques, numériques et climatiques. « Investir dans la santé, c’est investir dans la dignité humaine, dans la cohésion sociale, dans la réduction des inégalités et dans la stabilité de nos sociétés », a-t-il affirmé. Cette vision s’inscrit, selon lui, dans le cadre du nouveau Pacte pour la Méditerranée, qui place davantage les citoyens au cœur de la coopération entre les deux rives. Le ministre de la santé a, de son côté, estimé que la clôture du PASS III devait être considérée comme « le début d’une nouvelle étape de notre coopération avec l’Union européenne », alors que le Maroc poursuit la mise en œuvre de la réforme de son système de santé et du chantier de généralisation de la protection sociale. « Notre ambition est claire : construire un système plus équitable, plus performant et plus résilient », a-t-il déclaré, jugeant que cette transformation exige à la fois des investissements conséquents et des partenariats durables. Numérisation, souveraineté sanitaire et ressources humaines Les interventions des deux responsables ont convergé autour de plusieurs axes appelés à structurer la coopération future. La transformation numérique figure parmi les priorités identifiées. Amine Tehraoui a souligné l’importance de la gouvernance et de la valorisation des données de santé, devenues « des enjeux majeurs de performance, de qualité et de souveraineté ». Une orientation partagée par l’Union européenne, qui voit dans les systèmes d’information interopérables, la télémédecine et l’intelligence artificielle des leviers d’amélioration des soins et de réduction des inégalités territoriales. Autre chantier commun : la souveraineté pharmaceutique et vaccinale. Le ministre a rappelé que le Maroc dispose désormais d’une base industrielle solide et entend renforcer les partenariats favorisant l’innovation, la production locale et l’accès équitable aux produits de santé. L’Union européenne s’est dite prête à accompagner cette dynamique, notamment à travers le partage d’expertise, le renforcement des capacités réglementaires et le développement de partenariats industriels. Les deux parties ont également mis l’accent sur la sécurité sanitaire et la préparation aux crises futures. La pandémie de Covid-19 a montré, selon Dimiter Tzantchev, que les systèmes de santé sont interdépendants et que la coopération en matière de surveillance épidémiologique, de recherche et de gestion des risques doit être renforcée. Enfin, la question des ressources humaines apparaît comme un défi commun. « Sans femmes et hommes bien formés, reconnus et soutenus, aucune réforme ne peut réussir durablement », a rappelé l’ambassadeur européen. Une analyse partagée par le ministre, qui a plaidé pour un effort accru en matière de formation, de développement des compétences et de mobilité des professionnels de santé. Au terme de cette cérémonie, le PASS III apparaît ainsi comme une étape de transition. Si le programme s’achève officiellement, Rabat et Bruxelles ont clairement affiché leur intention de faire de la santé l’un des piliers du nouveau partenariat stratégique approfondi entre le Maroc et l’Union européenne, dans une logique davantage tournée vers l’innovation, la résilience et la souveraineté sanitaire. The post Clôture du PASS III : le Maroc et l’UE préparent l’après-réforme sanitaire appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: 2027: SDP ‘ll alleviate poverty, transform Nigeria’s future – Adebayo
items.description: Social Democratic Party (SDP) presidential candidate, Prince Adewole Adebayo, says the party will rescue Nigeria from poverty and insecurity. Adebayo ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‌‍‍‍⁠‌​‍​‌​stated this at the party’s September National Convention, entitled: “Consolidating the blueprint for a new Nigeria to secure our homeland and defeat poverty”, on Wednesday in Abuja. He maintained that Nigeria’s immense natural resources were divinely provided to guarantee prosperity for the country. On the SDP core mission, Adebayo emphasised the party stood apart from other political platforms because its members were driven by collective nation-building rather than personal self-glorification. He drew a historical parallel with the aborted 1993 presidential election widely believed to have been won by the late Chief MKO. Abiola, noting that the poverty the party fought to defeat decades ago had since grown and consumed citizens. ​”The poverty that SDP fought with Nigerians’ mandate to defeat and eradicate in 1993, that poverty has grown up and has consumed babies,” he stated, stressing the urgent need for a unified national rescue mission. Addressing the country’s current economic struggles, the presidential candidate argued that Nigeria’s under-development was not a result of a scarcity of natural wealth, but a failure of visionary governance. According to him, Nigeria possesses enough oil, gas and other mineral deposits to rival and surpass major global economies. ​”If God wanted us to be poor, he would not deposit under us sufficient minerals that no civilisation in human history had got before,” Adebayo asserted. He outlined a grassroots strategy focused on door-to-door mobilisation to win the hearts and minds of every day citizens. The presidential candidate urged party members to reject politics driven by personal enrichment and instead, focus on uniting the country ahead of the upcoming elections. ​”Our intention is known to God, and it’s simply that we will get Nigerians to accept that we don’t desire to be poor, and we don’t desire to die of insecurity. Everything we need to succeed is already here,” he said. The Vice-Presidential candidate of the party, Prof. Usman Bugaje, reinforced the party’s reformist stance. Bugaje warned that the country might face critical threats if citizens continued to value transactional ‘big man’ politics over genuine structural change. He noted that the party’s framework required individuals who were committed to national transformation rather than financial gains or superficial party size metrics. ​”People should be here not because they want money; people should be here because they want this ten-page change,” Bugaje stated, challenging the conventional Nigerian political obsession with labelling parties as “big” or “small.” He called for absolute integrity, sacrifice and ideological clarity among party faithful to steer the country away from its current challenges. items.title: Poor transport and storage systems contribute to post-harvest losses in Ghana – Mathias Yabe
items.description: The absence of appropriate transportation and storage systems is contributing to post-harvest losses among farmers, particularly those dealing with highly perishable crops, social entrepreneur and innovator Mathias Charles Yabe has said. Speaking on the 13th edition of the Loud and Green X-Space on JoyNews, Mr Yabe said the transportation of fresh produce could result in significant losses before the food reached consumers. He cited the experience of a lettuce farmer near the Dodowa Road who supplies produce to a buyer in Spintex. According to him, the farmer previously transported the lettuce by Aboboya to a lorry station before continuing the journey by trotro. He said the produce could break and wilt during the journey, significantly reducing the farmer’s earnings. “If the farmer is expecting to make GH¢1,500, by the time she gets to the buyer, she may end up with about GH¢700,” he said. Mr Yabe, however, said the losses should not simply be blamed on the farmer but should be viewed as evidence of the need for better systems to move perishable produce from farms to markets. As part of efforts to address the challenge, Agrofresh introduced a solar-powered refrigerated tricycle. “We recently introduced solar-powered refrigerated tricycles. These tricycles are a complementary solution to the stationary and then the mobile refrigerated units,” he said. Mr Yabe said the tricycle was piloted in collaboration with the Netherlands Embassy, Holland Green Tech and Eden Tree. He said one of the farmers who participated in the pilot reported no losses while using the refrigerated tricycle to deliver produce. “The farmer reported zero losses when she used our tricycle for the delivery,” he said. The intervention forms part of Agrofresh’s broader efforts to reduce post-harvest losses through solar-powered refrigeration. Mr Yabe said the company also builds refrigeration units that can be installed on farms and in communities to preserve fresh produce for longer periods. “Basically, we are building fridges on farms and in communities. Essentially, these fridges are supposed to help preserve food and extend its shelf life, especially fruits and vegetables, from five days to up to 21 days,” he said. He said the initiative was particularly relevant to farming communities where limited access to electricity made conventional refrigeration difficult to deploy. The discussion, which examined opportunities emerging from Ghana’s climate challenges, formed part of the 13th edition of the Loud and Green X-Space.

items.title: 24 die, many hospitalised after consuming herbal drinks in Ondo
items.description: By Dayo Johnson Akure Twenty-four persons have reportedly died while others were hospitalised in Araromi Obu and Odigbo towns in Odigbo Council Area of Ondo State, following suspected food poisoning. The incident, which occurred last weekend, has triggered anger in the affected communities. Youths took to the streets to protest the deaths and marched to the palace of the traditional ruler of Araromi Obu, Oba Rufus Akinrinmade, demanding urgent action to prevent further loss of lives. Eight deaths were recorded in Araromi Obu, while 16 were recorded in Odigbo town. Sources said the fatalities may be linked to the consumption of poisonous substances suspected to be contained in sachet herbal concoctions. Some of the deceased reportedly died in their homes, while others died in their sleep. Addressing the protesters, the traditional ruler of the community, Oba Akinrinmade, appealed for calm and assured them that efforts would be made to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the deaths and provide a lasting solution. The Permanent Secretary, Ondo State Ministry of Health, Dr. Ayodele Adiji, said preliminary findings suggested a possible link between the deaths and the consumption of locally brewed alcoholic beverages. Adiji specifically mentioned a locally produced drink as well as other herbal and ethanol-based drinks. He added that laboratory analysis of samples collected was ongoing to establish a direct connection. In response, the Chairman of Odigbo Local Government, Hon. Taiwo Adegoroye, imposed a one-month ban on the sale and consumption of locally brewed herbal drinks in the area as a precautionary measure. Adegoroye said a preliminary verbal autopsy by the council’s health team indicated a possible link between the deaths and the substances. He warned that anyone found selling or distributing the banned drinks during the restriction period would face arrest and prosecution. The State Commissioner for Health, Dr. Banji Ajaka, said investigations were underway to determine the actual cause of the deaths. Ajaka added that government was taking the matter seriously and would provide further details after assessments in the affected communities. Health authorities have urged residents to avoid consuming suspicious herbal concoctions or unverified sachet products pending the outcome of investigations. The Police spokesperson in the state, DSP Jimoh Abayomi, said that the command in collaboration with the government and relevant health authorities, have commenced a comprehensive investigation into the incidents with a view to determining the actual cause of the reported deaths. Abayomi noted that ” police personnel including Police Medical Services are working closely with officials of the Ondo State Ministry of Health and the Odigbo Local Government health authorities in the collection of relevant information and evidence, while medical and toxicological examinations are being conducted to ascertain the substance, if any, responsible for the fatalities. He cautioned “members of the public against spreading unverified information or attributing the deaths to any particular substance, as the investigation and laboratory analyses are still ongoing. “The actual number of casualties and the precise cause of the deaths will be established through the ongoing investigation. Abayomi advised “residents of the affected communities to remain calm and cooperate with the authorities by providing useful information that may assist the investigation. ” Members of the public are also urged to refrain from consuming unregulated or suspicious alcoholic and herbal preparations pending the outcome of the investigation. He said that “the Command is committed to unraveling the circumstances surrounding the unfortunate incidents and will take appropriate action against anyone found culpable. “The Command will continue to liaise with the Ondo State Government and relevant agencies and will provide further updates as soon as credible findings emerge. The post 24 die, many hospitalised after consuming herbal drinks in Ondo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: NELFUND has provided financial relief to less privileged – Shettima
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru The Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima, has described the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) established by the administration of President Bola Tinubu as a landmark initiative that has provided crucial financial relief to the children of the poor and removed the financial barriers to higher education. The administration, according to him, positioned the Fund as a vital social equalizer and a primary mechanism for poverty alleviation as well the advancement of education in Nigeria. Senator Shettima stated this on Wednesday in Abuja during an audience with the management team of the University of Abuja, led by the Vice Chancellor, Prof. Hakeem Babatunde Fawehinmi. The Vice President said that by ensuring tuition fees are covered and providing monthly upkeep allowances, the scheme—which targets students from less-privileged backgrounds who would otherwise be excluded from tertiary education—has ensured that poverty is no longer an excuse not to go to school. Recalling his days as student at the University of Maiduguri when the price of food surged at the cafeteria, he said the “NELFUND is a very beautiful initiative by the leadership of this country under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, created to give respite breathing space to the children of the poor.” VP Shettima also observed that Nigeria has crossed the rubicon and is firmly on the path of sustainable economic development under the Tinubu administration. He cited the recent upgrade of Nigeria’s sovereign credit ratings and outlooks by global rating agencies, attributing the success to stronger foreign exchange reserves, higher oil production, increased federal allocation following the removal of oil subsidy, and the ongoing macroeconomic reforms undertaken by the Renewed Hope administration. He applauded the management of the University of Abuja under the leadership of Prof. Fawehinmi, saying the Vice Chancellor has provided leadership that has surmounted the challenges that confronted the school in the past. The University of Abuja, he observed, is now standing on a solid pedestal, as real stability has been restored in the institution, even as he pledged that the federal government will do everything within its ability to give the school the needed support. Earlier, the Vice Chancellor of the University of Abuja, Prof. Fawehinmi commended Vice President Shettima for supporting and spearheading the growth and developmental strides of the Tinubu administration. The Vice Chancellor described VP Shettima as a mentor whose leadership qualities have assisted the University’s Governing Board to manage the school, even as he sought the institution’s partnership with the government to move the country forward. “We have always known you to be a highly cerebral and dynamic leader. We appreciate the generous strides you are making in the country. We are not surprised at your intellectual agility,” he stated. Prof. Fewehinmi said NELFUND, under the Renewed Hope Agenda of President Tinubu, has assisted immensely in bringing relative stability in the nation’s education sector, pointing out that students are able to go to school and are able to sustain their stay in the school.” He stated that the management as well as the Governing Council of the University of Abuja deemed it necessary to thank the Vice President for the support he has always given to the school. “Our recent history in terms of leadership has not been very palatable. There have been issues to do with our checkered history, but in the last eight months when we came on board, we tried our very best to stabilize the university,” he explained. The post NELFUND has provided financial relief to less privileged – Shettima appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Partisan MMDCE elections could stifle development – NDC
items.description: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has defended government’s position against fully partisan elections for Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs), arguing that such an arrangement could undermine development at the local level. Deputy Director of Elections and Information Technology of the NDC, Rashid Tanko Computer, said Ghana’s political culture makes it risky to have MMDCEs from a political party different from the party controlling central government. Speaking on Joy FM Top Story on Wednesday, September 9, he cited the possibility of an opposition MMDCE being elected in major cities such as Kumasi or Accra while a different political party controls central government. “Imagine you have His Excellency John Dramani Mahama and the NDC government in place, and then you are going to have an NPP man being an MCE in Kumasi or Accra. What do you expect? What kind of correlation are you going to have? It’s going to stifle development,” he stated. According to him, Ghana’s system of local governance must take into account the country’s political culture and traditions rather than simply adopting governance models from Western countries. “We can’t just go and borrow the democracy practices in the Western world and come and implement it in totality. We will have difficulties in implementing major decisions and other things, because you know the politics we do in Ghana,” he said. Mr Tanko Computer further defended government’s proposed model for selecting MMDCEs, insisting it would still give residents a meaningful opportunity to choose their local leaders. Under the proposed arrangement, five candidates would first be selected and subjected to interviews by the Public Services Commission. Three candidates would then proceed to the final stage, where residents within the district would vote to select their MMDCE. He said the proposed system is significantly different from the current arrangement, under which the President nominates an individual and assembly members vote on the nominee. “This one government has no role in it. And then they will now go and have universal suffrage within the district of which they are going to preside over, and they will decide their seat over there. It’s not the assemblymen who will now decide the seat. So it’s completely different,” he said. Mr Tanko Computer maintained that the proposed system seeks to balance democratic participation with the need for effective coordination between local and central government. His defence follows the Trades Union Congress (TUC) rejecting government’s proposal for the selection of MMDCEs, insisting that districts must be allowed to independently choose their leaders.

items.title: TUC urges Mahama to keep constitutional reform discussions open
items.description: The Trades Union Congress (TUC) is urging President John Mahama to keep discussions on the proposed constitutional reforms open to allow for broader consultation and consensus-building. Deputy Secretary-General of the TUC, Dr Kwabena Nyarko Otoo, said the union intends to engage the President and members of the constitutional reform implementation committee to further present its views on some of the recommendations. Speaking on Joy FM Top Story on Wednesday, September 9, Dr Otoo said the union also intends to engage the chairperson and members of the constitutional reform implementation committee to persuade them to reconsider some of the proposals. “We continue to appeal to the government not to foreclose the discussions. There are still more people with varying opinions, and it is important that we hear everything, everybody,” he said. He said the ultimate goal should be to build broad consensus around a reformed Constitution that strengthens Ghana’s democracy and contributes to the country’s economic and social transformation. Dr Nyarko Otoo also said the TUC disagrees with concerns that allowing the election of mayors along partisan political lines could threaten Ghana’s unity. He argued that several African countries, including Nigeria, Kenya and Senegal, elect local government leaders through partisan political processes without undermining their national cohesion. “The fear that electing a mayor for Kumasi or Ho, who is different, with a different political persuasion from the governing party, will break up the country, is an unfounded fear.” According to Dr Otoo, Ghana’s democratic development should extend to the grassroots, particularly in local governance. He maintained that partisan local elections could provide an opportunity to deepen democracy and improve the effectiveness of local governance. “We need to have absolute democracy at all levels,” he said. Dr Otoo said the TUC will continue to dialogue with government on the matter and plans to formally write to President Mahama to seek an audience.

items.title: Comoé : Deux adolescents meurent par noyade dans une retenue d’eau à Niangoloko
items.description: BURKINA-COMOE-NOYADE-ADOLESCENTS Comoé : Deux adolescents meurent par noyade dans une retenue d'eau à Niangoloko Niangoloko, 9 sept. 2026 (AIB)-Deux adolescents, âgés de 14 et 17 ans et issus d'une même famille, ont trouvé la mort par noyade, mardi soir, dans une retenue d'eau de Niangoloko, alors qu'ils étaient partis y pêcher. Selon des témoignages recueillis sur place, les deux frères étaient en train de pêcher lorsque le plus jeune est accidentellement tombé dans l'eau. En tentant de lui porter secours, son grand frère s'est à son tour retrouvé en difficulté. Malgré ses efforts, il n'a pas pu sauver son cadet, et les deux adolescents ont péri par noyade. Alertée, la Brigade nationale de sapeurs-pompiers (BNSP) de Banfora est intervenue pour repêcher les corps des victimes. Après les constatations d'usage effectuées par le commissariat de police de district (CPD) de Niangoloko, les dépouilles ont été remises à la famille pour inhumation. En cette période de saison des pluies, la BNSP appelle les parents à sensibiliser davantage leurs enfants sur les dangers liés aux cours et retenues d'eau. Elle invite également la population à faire preuve de la plus grande prudence aux abords des points d'eau. Agence d'information du Burkina BBH/no/ata
