items.title: Does Trump Want Republicans to Win the Midterms?
items.description: Is Donald Trump trying to help Republicans win the midterm elections? The obvious answer to this question is yes, of course , simply because all political leaders benefit from their party winning elections. Yet several of Trump’s actions throw this normally perfunctory question into at least some doubt. Traditionally, candidates laboring under the burden of an unpopular president seek to detach themselves from the national brand. Trump is making this impossible. He has launched a national ad campaign focused on himself, and thrown a high-profile “midterm convention” designed to further reinforce the synonymity of the party and its leader. Trump has also made several remarks that convey an emotional detachment from the election’s outcome—comments such as “I’m not affected by the election” or “I don’t care about the midterms.” Perhaps he is merely feigning indifference. Maybe he truly does not care. More likely, Trump cares about the outcome, but not enough to permit Republicans to acknowledge his lack of popularity. His approach, at any rate, nicely illustrates the drawbacks of handing total control of a political party to an egomaniac. Midterm elections have historically disfavored the president’s party. Candidates for office who are running in neutral or hostile territory accordingly tend to emphasize their differences with the president—think of Joe Manchin running an ad in West Virginia in 2010 showing him firing an actual bullet at Barack Obama’s cap-and-trade bill, or the Republican Will Hurd in 2018 criticizing Trump’s racism and affinity for Russia. [ Listen: Trump’s economy goes to the polls ] Trump’s public standing is unusually dire. He is currently polling far worse than either he did at this point in 2018 or Joe Biden did four years ago. In theory, this ought to give Republicans an especially strong incentive to edge away from Trump and emphasize local themes in their elections. Trump has decided to block this escape route. He is commandeering earned media with his “Trumpapalooza” show, drawing attention to the person endangered Republicans desperately need their constituents to forget. He has hoarded the party’s ad budget, warning Republicans, “This is my money that I control,” and that he would spend it on “Republicans that I think are good,” which is to say, slavishly loyal. He has promised to barnstorm the country, telling reporters, “I’ll be making a lot of stops,” including in Alaska, where the Republican Dan Sullivan is trailing. There is an old Simpsons episode in which the elderly oligarch Montgomery Burns informs the obsequious Smithers that, upon his own death, his loyal aide will be buried alive at his boss’s feet. Trump appears to be thinking along similar lines. This self-defeating behavior makes a degree of sense if you accept that Trump’s interest in politics is purely egocentric. He has difficulty caring about anything that does not directly involve himself, and the prospect of Republicans holding seats by repudiating his record is likely unpalatable. The benefits of same-party control of Congress are also smaller for Trump than other presidents, because he governs mainly through executive action. To the extent that a Democratic majority in either chamber might threaten him with oversight, he will surely disregard it, as he did during his first term. Although he finds Republican majorities preferable, the size of those majorities matters to him far less than their composition—a fully loyal minority may seem preferable to a fractious majority. What makes less sense is the willingness of many Republicans to cooperate with a strategy that consigns many of them to defeat. Consider, for instance, Mike Rogers, the Republican Senate candidate in Michigan. Rogers came up through politics long before Trump entered it, and is trying to win office in a state where the president’s approval rating is 25 points underwater. A recent poll of the state found Trump’s endorsement made voters less likely, by a 55 percent to 27 percent margin, to support a candidate. Yet Rogers has opened no daylight whatsoever with the unpopular president, even echoing his false claims of having the 2020 election stolen from him. When Trump launched a trade war with Canada, a move that poses an especially dire threat to Rogers’s own state, he declined to take the opportunity to display independence. Instead, he issued a statement mumbling his approval. (“President Trump is right to put America First—and tariffs are necessary, but are not a one-size-fits-all solution . ”) The same dynamic is occurring in other races, where Trump is throwing himself behind incumbents who are in danger mainly because voters don’t like him. [ Read: Trump plans to buy midterm ads about his own record ] To be sure, some Republicans subscribe to the theory that the Trump era has suspended normal midterm election dynamics. According to this account, a decisive sliver of voters are loyal to Trump, and not his party. Republicans can win only by enticing them to vote, which means making the election about their hero. “We’ve seen that a lot of Trump voters—they will crawl over glass to vote for the president,” one Republican strategist explained to Politico . Yet Trump has tried before to insert himself into non-presidential elections. And his efforts have mostly failed—not only in the 2018 midterms, when he refused to lie low, but also in multiple off-schedule elections (the most famous case being Georgia’s 2021 Senate runoff, which he made into a referendum on his effort to overturn the 2020 election). In the Trump era, his party has fared well only when it has been able to focus on the shortcomings of unpopular Democratic opponents, such as Hillary Clinton in 2016 and Biden and Kamala Harris in 2024. Making elections about Trump—which also occurred when he ran for reelection in 2020—has been a losing gambit. The political tip sheets in recent days have been filled with the lamentations of fatalistic Republican operatives. “We have no choice. We’re stuck on the boat with him whether we like it or not,” a top Republican campaign official confessed to Axios . They cannot stop Trump from staging Trumpapalooza, so they are reduced to praying for low ratings. “My only hope is that no one watches it since it’s competing versus NFL opening games,” a person close to the White House told Politico . “Hopefully nobody notices the embarrassing show.” Republicans are cooperating in a strategy that sacrifices their best chance of political survival, because the past decade has trained them to believe that resistance to Trump is futile. Trump did far less damage to the country during his first term, both because institutions and norm-following officials restrained him, and because his pathological instincts frequently undermined his support. The former limitation has broken down in the second term, but the latter one remains. Trump’s support has collapsed in large part because of his own poor choices.

items.title: Khadim Mboup, le « Génie en herbe » est devenu grand
items.description: En 2014, devant la présentatrice de l’émission Oumy Ndour, il avait donné une réponse avant même que la question ne fût achevée. Valdiodio Ndiaye. Vingt points. Une fulgurance qui avait fait de Khadim Mboup l’un des visages les plus familiers du tournoi national de « Génies en herbe ». Douze ans ont passé. Le jeune prodige de Louga a grandi, étudié à Lyon, Lausanne et au Québec. Les mathématiques ont rencontré l’économie. Et derrière les diplômes, une conviction s’est précisée : le Sénégal ne manque pas de cerveaux, il lui manque encore les moyens de les faire éclore, de les retenir, de les mettre au service de son propre destin. En 2014, sur la scène de la finale nationale de « Génies en herbe », Khadim Mboup livrait un récital de culture générale dont le souvenir n’a pas disparu. Mais derrière le champion que le petit écran avait révélé, il y avait un garçon que l’école avait patiemment façonné. En 2026, Khadim ne répond plus à la manière du garçon de 2014. Il regarde plus loin. « Ce qui me revient immédiatement, ce n'est pas tant la finale elle-même que ce qui s'est passé après », dit-il. Après, plusieurs élèves venaient lui demander comment devenir « cultivés », comment travailler, comment progresser. C’est cette image qui lui est restée. Pas le trophée. Pas les caméras : « Ça m'a fait réaliser que cette compétition n'avait pas seulement une valeur pour moi ou pour mon lycée. Elle inspirait ». Né à Genève, Khadim est profondément façonné par Louga où il grandit. L’enfant fréquente l’école coranique avant de rejoindre l’école sénégalaise. Cette première formation, il en parle encore. « C'est un ensemble de choses qui se sont conjuguées : mes parents, l'environnement familial, une curiosité qui était sans doute déjà là en moi, mais surtout l'éducation que m'a donnée ma grand-mère et mon passage à l'école coranique », explique-t-il. Pourtant, Khadim n’a pas suivi une route scolaire parfaitement rectiligne. Il a dû rattraper trois années, sauter des classes pour se mettre à niveau. En classe de quatrième, on décide de le présenter au Bfem comme candidat libre. Il termine premier de son centre d’examen. « Je pense que c'est là que quelque chose a basculé en moi », se souvient-il. Après, tout s’enchaîne. La série S. Les mathématiques. Le Concours général sénégalais où il obtient une distinction. Puis « Génies en herbe », remporté en 2014 avec le lycée Malick Sall. Le baccalauréat S1 avec mention. Des réussites qui pourraient donner l’illusion d’une trajectoire sans heurts. Lui-même récuse cette lecture trop simpliste. « Il n'y a pas eu un déclic isolé, séparé du reste. C'est venu naturellement, comme un prolongement de tout ce qui m'avait construit jusque-là », explique-t-il. Il comprend que ses études peuvent le conduire bien au-delà des frontières du Sénégal. Alors il part. Lyon d’abord, à l’Université Claude Bernard, pour des études scientifiques. Puis Lausanne, en Suisse, pour les mathématiques. Enfin le Québec, à l’Université Laval, où les mathématiques se frottent à l’économie. Une géographie universitaire qui aurait pu éloigner le jeune Lougatois de ses premières attaches. « Ce que j'ai ressenti surtout, c'est le besoin de rester moi-même », raconte-t-il. Il arrive dans des environnements universitaires exigeants sans se présenter en élève venu de loin qu’il faudrait d’abord rassurer. Il vient pour apprendre. Découvrir. Comprendre. S’imprégner. « Je suis resté sénégalais, avec cette même soif de savoir qui m'animait depuis l'école coranique et Génies en herbe », confie-t-il. Patriotisme Depuis l’étranger, Khadim Mboup mesure davantage l’étendue du potentiel sénégalais. Il voit les talents. Les capacités d’innovation. La jeunesse. Il voit aussi les lenteurs, les insuffisances, les occasions manquées. Il parle de formation scientifique, de réformes, de la place de la science, de la manière d’enseigner. Il parle aussi de la décolonisation de l’éducation, de la façon dont le savoir est transmis, des connaissances que l’on choisit de valoriser. Ce n’est plus le candidat de « Génies en herbe » qui parle. C’est un jeune scientifique devenu économiste, un Sénégalais qui a vu d’autres systèmes universitaires et qui revient par la pensée vers celui qui l’a formé. Il ne dit pas que tout est à refaire. Il dit que beaucoup reste à faire. Le Sénégal, estime le champion, ne propose pas encore suffisamment d’offres de formation scientifique de haut niveau. Mais le problème va plus loin. Même des diplômés issus d’écoles d’excellence sénégalaises, comme l’École Polytechnique de Thiès ou l’École nationale de la statistique et de l’analyse économique (Ensae), finissent par partir après leur formation. Khadim y voit une contradiction : « On investit dans la formation de ces jeunes, mais on ne construit pas les conditions pour les retenir ni les mécanismes pour les intégrer directement au service du pays. » Son interrogation est concrète. Pourquoi les diplômés de l’École nationale d’administration (Ena) bénéficient-ils d’une prise en charge par l’État et d’un parcours professionnel dans la fonction publique alors que les diplômés des filières scientifiques et techniques ne disposent pas du même cadre ? La question n’est pas théorique. Elle concerne ceux qui devront demain bâtir les infrastructures, produire les statistiques, concevoir les modèles économiques, penser les politiques publiques. « Ce sont pourtant ces profils, ingénieurs, statisticiens, économistes, mathématiciens, dont le Sénégal a le plus besoin pour bâtir ses infrastructures, penser ses politiques publiques avec rigueur et accélérer sa transformation économique », affirme-t-il. Il faut donc, selon lui, cesser de faire du retour au pays une simple affaire de volonté individuelle. Le jeune diplômé parti à l’étranger n’est pas nécessairement quelqu’un qui tourne le dos à son pays. Il peut être quelqu’un qui cherche les conditions de son propre accomplissement. Il y a son engagement, oui. Son désir de mettre ses compétences en mathématiques et en économie au service du développement du Sénégal. Mais il y a aussi la responsabilité de l’État de créer les conditions qui rendront ce choix possible. « Tant que cette cohérence n'existe pas, on continuera à demander à des jeunes de revenir sacrifier des opportunités, sans leur offrir en retour un cadre à la hauteur de leur formation », avertit-il. Entre-temps, les mathématiques ont changé de place dans son esprit. Elles ne sont plus seulement la discipline dans laquelle il excellait. Elles sont devenues un outil. Lorsqu’il se tourne vers l’économie à l’Université Laval, Khadim ne tourne pas le dos aux nombres. Il les emmène avec lui. « Je ne vois pas ce passage comme un abandon des mathématiques, mais comme un prolongement naturel », précise-t-il. Soif d’apprendre et de comprendre Le garçon qui cherchait les réponses aux questions de culture générale s’intéresse désormais aux mécanismes qui façonnent la vie des sociétés. Et lorsqu’il regarde le Khadim de 2014, il ne renie rien. « Ce qui n'a jamais changé, c'est l'essentiel : cette soif d'apprendre et de comprendre, cette rigueur héritée de l'école coranique, et cette spiritualité qui m'accompagne partout où je vais », dit-il. Il est resté Sénégalais. Resté talibé. Resté curieux. Resté calme. Mais quelque chose a changé dans son regard. Élève, il apprenait pour réussir. Pour aller plus loin dans ses études. Aujourd’hui, le savoir porte une autre charge. Cette même soif de savoir s'est transformée en une volonté de comprendre les grands enjeux du Sénégal et de l'Afrique, et surtout en une envie de servir, de mettre tout ce parcours au profit de son pays. Voilà le chemin parcouru. Le reste est encore à écrire. Khadim Mboup ne parle pas de son avenir en termes de carrière personnelle. Il parle de transformation. D’un Sénégal capable de compter sur ses propres forces, de construire une économie endogène et souveraine, de donner à ses jeunes les moyens de leurs rêves. À ses yeux, le pays regorge de talents, de jeunes brillants, mais qu'il manque encore les structures pour les révéler, les former et les retenir. « Je veux m'engager concrètement auprès de la jeunesse sénégalaise, essayer humblement de montrer, à travers mon propre parcours imparfait, qu'il est possible de viser l'excellence sans jamais renier ses racines », lance Khadim. Par Adama NDIAYE

items.title: Bougouriba/Bondigui : autorités et populations mobilisées contre les gîtes larvaires
items.description: Bougouriba/Bondigui : autorités et populations mobilisées contre les gîtes larvaires Bondigui, 8 septembre 2026 (AIB)- Les autorités locales et les populations de la commune de Bondigui se sont mobilisées, samedi 5 et dimanche 6 septembre 2026, dans le cadre de la deuxième phase des Journées nationales de lutte anti-vectorielle (JN-LAV), consacrée à la réduction des gîtes larvaires et à la prévention du paludisme. L’activité a mobilisé les services d’hygiène et d’assainissement de la mairie, le personnel de santé, les Forces de défense et de sécurité (FDS), des commerçants, des jeunes ainsi que des leaders religieux. Après une première phase marquée par une forte adhésion des populations, cette deuxième étape a notamment permis de constater et de vérifier la mise en œuvre effective des actions d’assainissement engagées dans la commune. Les équipes déployées sur le terrain ont parcouru plusieurs artères de Bondigui à la recherche de potentiels gîtes larvaires. Elles ont procédé à leur destruction et sensibilisé les populations sur les bonnes pratiques d’assainissement. Des pneus usagés, susceptibles de retenir les eaux de pluie et de favoriser la prolifération des moustiques, ont notamment été collectés et détruits le long de certaines voies. Les opérations ont également porté sur les caniveaux, dont l’entretien et le curage contribuent à limiter la stagnation des eaux et, partant, la formation de gîtes larvaires. L’infirmier chef de poste (ICP) du Centre de santé et de promotion sociale (CSPS) de Bondigui, Salia Dao, a rappelé que le paludisme demeure l’une des principales causes de morbidité et de mortalité au Burkina Faso. Selon lui, la période hivernale constitue une période particulièrement favorable à la multiplication des gîtes larvaires, d’où la nécessité de renforcer les actions préventives au sein des communautés. Dans les domiciles, les équipes ont également sensibilisé les ménages sur l’importance de maintenir leur environnement propre et de supprimer tout objet ou récipient susceptible de retenir de l’eau. Les populations ont notamment été invitées à se débarrasser des jarres, bidons, pneus et autres ustensiles abandonnés. Des démonstrations pratiques de destruction des gîtes larvaires ont été réalisées afin de permettre aux habitants de mieux maîtriser les gestes simples à adopter au quotidien pour limiter la prolifération des moustiques vecteurs du paludisme. Pour les acteurs de la lutte anti-vectorielle, l’implication des communautés constitue un maillon essentiel dans la réduction durable du paludisme et dans l’atteinte de l’objectif national d’élimination de la maladie à l’horizon 2030. Le responsable du service d’hygiène et d’assainissement de la mairie de Bondigui, Domondiele Pascal Hien, a exhorté les populations à maintenir leur cadre de vie propre. « Rendre propre son cadre de vie, c’est se protéger et protéger son entourage contre le paludisme », a-t-il déclaré, invitant les habitants à faire de la lutte contre les gîtes larvaires une pratique quotidienne. Il a également appelé les populations à s’approprier durablement les Journées nationales de lutte anti-vectorielle afin de faire de l’assainissement un réflexe collectif dans la commune. Agence d'Information du Burkina HDP/kmg/ata

items.title: Diphtheria: No outbreak in Lagos – Abayomi
items.description: By Chioma Obinna The Lagos state Commissioner for Health, Prof Akin Abayomi on Wednesday raised its disease surveillance and preparedness against diphtheria, warning residents not to panic but to remain vigilant as the outbreak continues to spread in parts of Nigeria. Abayomi, however, said there is currently no outbreak of diphtheria in Lagos, despite recording 53 suspected cases in 2026, six of which were laboratory-confirmed. The Commissioner, who gave the assurance at a media briefing on the state’s diphtheria preparedness and response, said the government was taking precautionary measures because of the high level of movement between Lagos and states currently battling the disease. According to him, the situation requires vigilance because Lagos’ huge population and extensive connections with other parts of the country could facilitate community transmission if imported cases are not detected and managed early. “We are appealing to all Lagosians to remain calm. There is no current outbreak of diphtheria in Lagos. We are simply taking precautionary measures,” Abayomi said. The Commissioner said the government was particularly concerned about the outbreak reported in states including Kano, Katsina, Kaduna, Benue and Zamfara, noting that the continuous movement of people between Lagos and affected areas made surveillance imperative. “We are watching this outbreak expand, and we are cautious in Lagos, as always. The Executive Council always likes to err on the side of caution and increase our prevention strategies in the state,” he said. Abayomi explained that diphtheria is a serious bacterial respiratory infection capable of causing life-threatening complications when treatment is delayed. He said the disease could produce a toxin capable of attacking the heart, while swelling and a thick membrane in the throat could obstruct breathing and swallowing. “There are two major things that happen to a patient with diphtheria. First, it can block the breathing apparatus in the throat, preventing the person from breathing normally or swallowing liquids and food properly. “Secondly, the toxin can enter the blood and travel to the heart, causing problems with the heartbeat and, eventually, heart failure.” He warned that an undiagnosed infection could therefore progress rapidly into airway obstruction and inflammation of the heart. Abayomi urged anyone developing severe sore throat, fever, weakness, neck swelling, difficulty breathing or swallowing, particularly after travelling to an affected state or having contact with a confirmed case, to seek medical attention immediately. “If you have any of these symptoms, present yourself quickly to one of our primary healthcare centres or your doctor so that we can make the diagnosis, carry out the necessary diagnostic workup and start treatment as quickly as possible,” he said. Giving an update on the situation in Lagos, Abayomi disclosed that 53 suspected diphtheria cases had been recorded in the state so far in 2026. Only six, he said, were confirmed through laboratory diagnosis, with all six cases appropriately managed. He added that contacts of confirmed patients were traced and placed under observation throughout the incubation period to detect possible secondary infections. “In Lagos, we have had sporadic cases of diphtheria. In fact, in 2026, we have had 53 suspected cases. Of those 53, only six have been confirmed through laboratory diagnosis,” he said. The Commissioner stressed that early diagnosis significantly improves the chances of successful treatment. “The treatment for diphtheria is very effective if the disease is diagnosed early,” Abayomi said, explaining that treatment involves antibiotics and medication capable of neutralising the toxin produced by the bacteria. While stressing that immunisation remains the most effective protection against diphtheria, Abayomi disclosed that only about 64 per cent of children in Lagos have received full vaccination coverage. He urged parents and guardians to check their children’s immunisation records and ensure that they receive all three doses of the pentavalent vaccine. “If you have received three doses, then you have significant protection. If you have received two, one or none, then you are vulnerable,” he warned. According to him, the three doses are expected to be administered at six, 10 and 14 weeks. He said Lagos has more than 1,000 healthcare facilities providing routine immunisation services across the public and private sectors, with vaccines available free at government facilities. The Commissioner clarified that primary healthcare centres are mainly vaccination points and are not the facilities designated to diagnose and manage suspected diphtheria cases. He listed the four designated centres as the Infectious Disease Hospital, Yaba; Massey Street Children’s Hospital, Lagos Island; Lagos University Teaching Hospital, LUTH; and Lagos State University Teaching Hospital, LASUTH. “If we suspect a case of diphtheria, we refer the patient to designated facilities. These are the four centres where we actively manage suspected cases of diphtheria. They have the capacity to make the diagnosis and manage the complications,” Abayomi said. He noted that severe cases could require advanced intervention to maintain the patient’s airway and close monitoring of the heart to prevent fatal complications. With schools expected to reopen soon, Abayomi said the Ministry of Health was working with the education sector to strengthen awareness and vaccination among schoolchildren. He said suspected cases in schools would trigger contact tracing and other infection-control measures. The Commissioner also urged residents to observe basic respiratory hygiene, including covering the mouth and nose when coughing or sneezing, washing hands regularly and avoiding close contact with others when experiencing respiratory symptoms. Speaking, the Permanent Secretary, Lagos State Ministry of Health, Dr. Dayo Lajide, also appealed to parents to ensure their children are fully vaccinated. “More importantly, we have to make sure that all our children are vaccinated,” Lajide said. She also urged the media to play a responsible role by providing accurate information to prevent unnecessary panic while encouraging residents to take appropriate preventive measures. She added that the government’s heightened surveillance was not a declaration of an outbreak in Lagos, but a precautionary response designed to ensure that any suspected case is detected, isolated, investigated and treated before it can trigger wider transmission. items.title: Ligue des champions: le FC Barcelone s'amuse face à Feyenoord
items.description: A l'image de ses débuts tonitruants en championnat d'Espagne, le FC Barcelone a parfaitement lancé sa Ligue des champions en surclassant le Feyenoord Rotterdam (5-1), grâce notamment à un doublé de Raphinha, mercredi au Camp Nou. Les Barcelonais, leaders de la Liga grâce à leur carton plein (4 victoires) et un total impressionnant de 17 buts, ont affiché la même efficacité offensive en C1 face aux Néerlandais. Il n'a fallu que trois minutes au capitaine blaugrana Raphinha pour ouvrir la marque. Trouvé par Lamine Yamal, l'actuel meilleur buteur de Liga (6 buts) a devancé un défenseur, puis en a éliminé deux autres grâce à une feinte du gauche, avant de loger une frappe au fond des filets. C'est ensuite l'une des recrues estivales du Barça, Karim Adeyemi, qui a assuré le spectacle en doublant la mise d'une superbe frappe enroulée du droit (22e). Après la pause, Raphinha, décidément inarrêtable en ce début de saison, s'est offert un doublé après un service parfait de Pedri (57e). Le champion du monde espagnol Lamine Yamal a corsé l'addition d'un magnifique coup franc (77e), avant d'offrir le cinquième but à la recrue Gabriel Jesus, buteur de la tête (85e). Feyenoord avait réduit le score par Sem Steijn (82e). Lors de la prochaine journée (13 octobre), le Barça se déplacera à Istanbul pour affronter Galatasaray avant d'aller se mesurer une semaine plus tard au Paris SG, double tenant du titre. The post Ligue des champions: le FC Barcelone s'amuse face à Feyenoord appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Raphinha bags brace as Barcelona demolish Feyenoord 5-1
items.description: Raphinha continued his superb goalscoring form with a brace as Barcelona demolished Feyenoord 5-1 to begin their Champions League campaign in perfect fashion on Wednesday. Karim Adeyemi curled home brilliantly from long range in between Raphinha’s strikes and Lamine Yamal bent in a free-kick as Hansi Flick’s team made light work of their Dutch visitors. After Sem Steijn pulled one back, Barca substitute Gabriel Jesus netted a fifth, the forward’s first goal since joining from Arsenal this summer. The Catalan giants, who last won the competition in 2015, have triumphed in all five of their matches across all competitions this season — and scored five goals in four of them. Winger Raphinha has been playing up front after Barca sold Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres, and has rapidly taken to his new position, plundering eight goals in five games. “Playing in front of our fans we always have to show perfect football, or nearly perfect, and with the support of the fans it’s a lot easier,” Barca captain Raphinha told Movistar. “I think we were very good, from the start of the game, controlling the game and with the chances we had we were able to score and it gives us a lot of confidence.” The Brazil international said that despite the club’s excellent start, there was still a long way to go. “In a season as long as this, there are many ups and downs,” added Raphinha. “Starting the season like this obviously gives us a lot of confidence and we have to continue like this. “We have to hope the downs are as small as possible.” Flick made five changes to the team that thrashed Valencia on Sunday in La Liga, although he maintained star attackers Yamal and Raphinha, as well as new arrival Rodri in his line-up. – Barca storm out of blocks – After days of baking weather in Barcelona, a storm broke ahead of the game, lashing rain down on the Camp Nou pitch and sending supporters scurrying for shelter. By the time it stopped pouring early in the first half, Barcelona were already ahead. Raphinha netted the opener after three minutes. The Brazilian was razor sharp to break into the box and cut inside, sending two defenders sliding the wrong way on the slick turf, before slotting home. Adeyemi, in for Anthony Gordon, doubled Barcelona’s lead with a superb strike from outside the area, bent beyond Feyenoord goalkeeper Tjark Ernst. Anis Hadj Moussa threatened for Feyenoord at the other end but Joan Garcia pushed out his shot at the near post. Barca kept generating openings and defender Joao Cancelo came close to adding a third when he skinned Givairo Read and crashed a shot against the outside of the post. Raphinha netted again before the hour mark for Barca’s third, running on to Pedri’s perfect through-ball and slotting home. The Dutch side thought they had pulled one back straight away when Nacho Ferri slotted home but it was disallowed after a VAR review for offside in the build-up. Yamal bagged Barca’s fourth, direct from a free-kick which crept through the wall, his first such strike for the club. Feyenoord sent on Shaqueel van Persie, the 19-year-old son of former Dutch international Robin van Persie, to try and salvage some pride. Steijn eventually pulled one back for the visitors when he escaped Jules Kounde and Goncalo Borges picked him out with a dangerous low cross to the back post. It was the only blot on Barca’s copy book on an otherwise strong start to their league phase, rounded off by Jesus’s glancing header from Yamal’s cross for the fifth. The post Raphinha bags brace as Barcelona demolish Feyenoord 5-1 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Goods transport owners demand release of containers seized by Islamabad police
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Goods transporters on Wednesday demanded that the Ministry of Interior release containers detained by Islamabad police ahead of the PTI’s scheduled Islamabad long march at the end of the month. The PTI, with the confidence and support of the opposition alliance — Tehreek-i-Tahaffuz Ayeen-i-Pakistan (TTAP) — has announced a long march towards Islamabad against what it calls the “illegal” detention of party founder and ex-premier Imran Khan and to demand his release. The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday decided to form a larger bench to hear a petition against the PTI’s planned protest, terming the matter sensitive and observing that it could have constitutional implications. In a statement on Wednesday, All Pakistan Goods Transport Owners Association President Muhammad Owais Chaudhry expressed concern over the seizure of container vehicles by Islamabad police, saying that the vehicles and containers should not be used for political purposes or to block roads during possible political activity on September 27. He said that around 100 container vehicles had been taken into custody from different areas of Islamabad, mainly Sangjani and Tarnol, the statement said. “The containers were being kept to possibly to block roads during the anticipated protest.” “What we demand is that there are a large number of containers available for rent in and around the federal capital — the Islamabad police or the administration should rent empty containers and use them as they wish,” Chaudhry was quoted as saying. He added that some impounded vehicles had reportedly been parked in deserted areas, while containers had allegedly been removed from certain vehicles, causing financial losses and business difficulties for their owners. “We had to facilitate the transporters in removing the goods from the containers — because the authorities do not take responsibility for the loss or damage to the cargo,” he added. Meanwhile, the association said it had received complaints from transporters alleging that some seized vehicles and containers were released after money was paid, while several others remained in police custody. It demanded a transparent investigation into the allegations and said the transporters had political affiliations on an individual basis. Their opposition to the impounding of vehicles, it added, should not be construed as a political link with the PTI, as the commercial vehicles were meant for trade and economic activity, “not for safety and security purposes of the police department”. The association also warned the government against impounding the vehicles, saying their forced use for political purposes created “an impression of state coercion”.

items.title: Apple unveils its first foldable smartphone iPhone Duo
items.description: Apple unveiled its long-awaited first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, on Wednesday, at the company’s first launch event since CEO John Ternus took the reins on September 1. Apple’s first foldable comes seven years after Samsung pioneered the category, but the American tech giant is expected to take a sizable chunk of the market. “Others have created foldables that just feel like two phones awkwardly stuck together,” Ternus said in a video shown at the Steve Jobs Theater at Apple’s headquarters in Cupertino, California. Apple wanted a device with a large display “that feels as natural and intuitive as (the) iPad,” said the former head of Apple’s hardware division, who succeeded Tim Cook this month. The format essentially combines the portability of a smartphone with the larger display of a tablet, offering users a bigger screen without carrying a tablet-sized device. Roughly the size and shape of a passport when folded, the iPhone Duo is made with titanium and has a 7.6-inch (19-centimeter) internal display and a 5.4-inch (14-centimeter) external display. It is available in two colors, “star white” and “night sky.” The Duo will go on sale in 70 countries beginning October 23, the company said. Apple touted the phone’s multiple cameras, including a front-facing external lens, two back-facing lenses and an internal lens. The lenses can be used simultaneously when the device is fully open. The Duo is priced starting at $1,999, slightly more than Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold8, which starts at around $1,899. Apple also announced a new monthly leasing program called Apple Upgrade, which lets customers pay off their purchase over one or two years. Samsung launched the industry’s first mainstream foldable smartphone, the Galaxy Fold, in 2019. Foldable smartphones make up a tiny fraction of the market, at less than 2 percent of global shipments, but Apple is expected to capture about a third of demand with its entry, according to research firm IDC. “Apple’s foldable iPhone is very likely to shift the competitive dynamics both in China and global markets,” IDC research associate Kiranjeet Kaur told AFP. items.title: Free tablets , missed opportunities ? Rethinking Ghana’s one student-one tablet initiative
items.description: Ghana’s digital education investment needs digital discipline to succeed. Ghana’s Free Senior High School (Free SHS) programme has significantly expanded access to secondary education. As the programme evolves, the government has complemented it with a major digital education intervention, which is the One Student–One Tablet initiative, announced in January, 2023 and formally launched on 25th March, 2024 under the Ghana Smart Schools Project. The initiative was designed to provide SHS and TVET students with tablets containing educational resources to support research, teaching and learning. The vision is undoubtedly commendable. But as a teacher and school counsellor, I believe we must now ask a more fundamental question: Are students using these tablets for the purpose for which they were provided? From my everyday interaction with students, it appears that although some use the devices productively, many spend considerable time on gaming, entertainment, social interaction, watching videos and other activities unrelated to their studies. This presents a paradox: we have successfully placed technology in the hands of students, but have we done enough to prepare them to use it responsibly? The problem is not the tablet. The tablet initiative is a brilliant intervention. Properly used, a single device can serve as an electronic library, research centre, classroom and repository of textbooks, past questions and other learning materials. The challenge is, therefore, not access to technology but digital behaviour. A student may pick up the tablet intending to research an academic topic and, within minutes, become distracted by entertainment, games or social media. Consequently, providing a device does not automatically produce better learning. Digital access must be accompanied by digital discipline. Students need digital literacy and self-regulation Adolescents require guidance in managing technology responsibly. Students must learn how to distinguish educational use from social use, manage screen time, evaluate online information, protect their privacy and maintain appropriate digital behaviour. This means that the One Student–One Tablet initiative should be viewed not merely as a technology programme but also as an educational, behavioural and counselling intervention. Schools should deliberately incorporate digital citizenship, responsible social media use, internet safety, time management, cyberbullying, digital ethics, information literacy and responsible use of artificial intelligence into their guidance and counselling programmes. Confiscation and punishment alone will not solve the problem. Students must be taught self-regulation. Teachers and parents have a responsibility! Teachers should not see the tablet merely as a device to monitor. It should be integrated into teaching through research assignments, electronic textbooks, past questions, educational videos, digital presentations and collaborative learning. Parents and guardians must equally reinforce responsible use at home by establishing reasonable expectations around study, entertainment and sleep. The responsibility therefore rests on government, schools, teachers, counsellors, parents, and students. The next question must be about impact. The government has made a substantial investment in digitalising education. The official objective of the Ghana Smart Schools Project is to use technology to enhance teaching and learning and equip students for a rapidly changing world. The next stage must, therefore, go beyond distribution. We must ask: Are students reading more? Are they researching more? Are students using the devices effectively? Are students becoming more digitally competent? And, ultimately, are learning outcomes improving? These questions should be answered through periodic national evaluations involving classroom observations, learner surveys and analyses of academic performance. The tablet is an opportunity, not a toy We must not demonise technology. Ghanaian students will graduate into a world in which digital competence, information literacy and technological adaptability are essential. Our responsibility is, therefore, not to keep students away from technology but to teach them how to control technology rather than allowing technology to control them. The Free SHS programme has opened the doors of secondary education to more Ghanaian children. The One Student–One Tablet initiative has the potential to open another door to digital learning. But that opportunity will only be realised when students understand that the tablet in their hands is not merely a possession or entertainment device; it is an investment in their education and future. The government has provided the device. The school must provide guidance. The teacher must provide the direction. The counsellor must provide the behavioural support. The parent must provide the reinforcement. The student must provide the discipline. Only then can Ghana move from Free SHS and free tablets to meaningful learning outcomes. Technology transforms education only when it transforms learning habits. The success of the One Student-One Tablet initiative will ultimately depend not on how many devices are distributed but on how wisely they are used. Thank you.

items.title: Mahama has not abandoned Haruna Iddrisu, he is backing him to fix education challenges – Spokesperson
items.description: The spokesperson for the Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, says President John Mahama has not abandoned the Minister to deal with challenges confronting Ghana’s education sector. According to Hashmin Mohammed, claims by former Manhyia North MP, Collins Owusu Amankwah, suggesting that the President had left Mr Iddrisu to struggle with challenges in the sector were “factually wrong, politically convenient and completely unsupported by the evidence”. In a statement, Mr Mohammed said attempts to portray challenges associated with the 2026 Computerised School Selection and Placement System (CSSPS) as evidence of presidential neglect were an effort to create a false political narrative. “The attempt to portray the challenges associated with the 2026 Computerised School Selection and Placement System (CSSPS) as evidence of presidential neglect is nothing more than an attempt to manufacture a political narrative where none exists,” he said. Mr Mohammed maintained that the CSSPS was functioning and undergoing reforms to address longstanding weaknesses and improve the experience of students, parents and schools. He said the Ministry of Education inherited a system that required significant reforms but had chosen to confront the challenges rather than continue blaming previous administrations. “The Hon. Minister has chosen to confront the problems head-on, strengthening the system, improving accountability and putting mechanisms in place to make placement more transparent, responsive and efficient,” he stated. According to him, the decentralisation of placement resolution centres was among the interventions introduced to bring assistance closer to parents and students and reduce the difficulties associated with resolving placement-related concerns. He argued that challenges associated with a complex national placement exercise should not automatically be interpreted as evidence of a lack of government support. Mr Mohammed stressed that President Mahama remained firmly behind Mr Iddrisu and the reforms being undertaken in the education sector. “President John Dramani Mahama did not appoint Hon. Haruna Iddrisu to fail. He appointed him to fix problems. And he is supporting him to do exactly that,” he said. He said the President’s support was reflected in government policies, resource allocation and interventions aimed at transforming the education sector. According to the spokesperson, the government is simultaneously addressing infrastructure deficits, expanding school capacity and improving access to teaching and learning materials. He said the objective was to create sufficient capacity in both Category A and Category B schools to ensure Ghanaian children were not denied access to quality secondary education because of inadequate infrastructure or limited school capacity. Mr Mohammed urged political actors to ensure that discussions surrounding education were based on facts rather than political convenience. “We appreciate the former MP’s interest in Ghana’s education sector. But public discourse on education must be based on facts, not political convenience,” he said. He added that presenting every challenge encountered during the implementation of a national programme as evidence of presidential failure would not contribute to solving the underlying problems. “The reality is that the Mahama administration inherited challenges across the education sector and has chosen to confront them through reform, investment and institutional strengthening,” he stated. Mr Mohammed maintained that the CSSPS was being improved rather than abandoned, while the Education Minister was receiving the necessary support to address challenges in the sector. “The CSSPS is being improved, not abandoned. The Education Minister is being supported, not isolated. And the education sector is being reformed, not left to drift,” he said. He insisted that President Mahama had given Mr Iddrisu the mandate, political backing and institutional support to address the problems he inherited. “Those who have genuine concerns about education are welcome to contribute constructive ideas. But attempts to turn every reform challenge into evidence of presidential abandonment will not change the facts,” he added. “The Government is fixing the system. The reforms are underway. And President Mahama remains firmly behind the Education Minister.”

items.description: ANKARA, Sept 9 (Reuters) - Pakistan has delivered a Saudi warning to Iran to rein in its Yemeni Houthi allies after they stepped up attacks on the kingdom, in a coordinated effort to prevent the crisis from spiralling, Saudi, Pakistani and Iranian sources said. items.title: Pandémies : le Sénégal mobilise 13,89 milliards de francs CFA pour renforcer sa riposte
items.description: Le Sénégal renforce son dispositif de prévention et de réponse aux pandémies. Le ministre de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique, Ibrahima Sy, a lancé, ce mercredi 09 septembre 2026, un projet triennal d’un montant global de 24,6 millions de dollars soit 13,89 milliards de francs CFA destiné à renforcer les capacités nationales de prévention, de préparation et de riposte face aux futures urgences sanitaires. Face à la multiplication des menaces sanitaires, le pays veut consolider son dispositif de prévention et de riposte. Il vient de lancer le projet « Renforcement des capacités de prévention, de préparation et de riposte aux pandémies », financé par le Pandemic Fund, pour une durée de trois ans. D’un montant global d’environ 24,6 millions de dollars, le programme repose sur l’approche « One Health » ou « Une seule santé ». Celle-ci vise à renforcer la coordination entre les secteurs de la santé humaine, de la santé animale et de l’environnement, considérés comme étroitement liés dans la prévention et la gestion des crises sanitaires. Pour le ministre de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique, Ibrahima Sy, cette initiative doit permettre au Sénégal de mieux faire face aux risques sanitaires présents et futurs. « Dans un monde où les crises sanitaires sont de plus en plus fréquentes, complexes et interconnectées, cette initiative marque un tournant décisif. Notre ambition est claire : bâtir un système de santé hautement résilient et plus préparé aux risques sanitaires présents et futurs », a-t-il déclaré. Surveillance, laboratoires et ressources humaines Le projet entend notamment renforcer la surveillance épidémiologique et les systèmes d’alerte précoce, les capacités des laboratoires ainsi que les ressources humaines. Trois axes considérés comme prioritaires pour améliorer la préparation du pays face aux éventuelles crises sanitaires. Ces objectifs doivent également permettre au Sénégal de progresser vers un niveau d’excellence en matière de surveillance, de diagnostic et de développement du capital humain, conformément aux exigences du Règlement sanitaire international. « C’est tout le sens du projet que nous consacrons aujourd’hui. Ce projet du Pandemic Fund va permettre de mettre en marche concrètement l’approche de la santé dans toutes les politiques et accélérer la réalisation de la couverture sanitaire universelle », a souligné Ibrahima Sy. Une approche multisectorielle Sous la coordination du ministère de la Santé et de l’Hygiène publique, le projet bénéficie de l’appui technique de plusieurs partenaires, dont la Banque mondiale, l’Organisation mondiale de la santé (OMS), la FAO et l’UNICEF. La coordinatrice sous-régionale de la FAO pour l’Afrique de l’Ouest, Bintia Stephen-Tchicaya, a insisté sur la nécessité d’une mobilisation collective pour assurer la réussite du programme. « Ce lancement n’est pas une fin en soi, mais c’est le point de départ d’une mise en œuvre exigeante qui nécessitera la mobilisation continue de tous : les autorités nationales, les partenaires techniques et financiers, les chercheurs, les communautés à la base et les sociétés civiles », a-t-elle indiqué. Elle estime que la réussite du projet dépendra notamment de la capacité des différents acteurs à dépasser les cloisonnements entre secteurs. De son côté, le représentant de l’UNICEF au Sénégal, Jacques Boyer, a réaffirmé l’engagement de son organisation aux côtés de l’État. « Au nom de l’UNICEF, je réaffirme notre soutien indéfectible aux côtés de l’État du Sénégal, dans un esprit de partenariat transparent et rigoureux, pour que chaque investissement consenti produise un impact durable au bénéfice des populations », a-t-il déclaré. À travers ce financement, le Sénégal entend ainsi consolider les acquis de son système de sécurité sanitaire et mieux anticiper les futures urgences. Les résultats du projet devront être capitalisés, partagés et réutilisés dans l’élaboration des politiques nationales de sécurité sanitaire. A.N

items.title: Apple debuts passport-shaped foldable phone, called Duo
items.description: Apple on Wednesday unveiled a foldable phone called Duo, introducing the biggest change in years in the company’s flagship product. The Duo is sized and shaped like a passport, with rounded edges. It opens into a horizontal, wide screen that can also be viewed vertically. There is a smaller single screen on the front when the phone is folded. When open, it is Apple’s thinnest phone, the company said. The folding phone event, the first with new Chief Executive Officer John Ternus at the helm, is the most noticeable overhaul of Apple’s flagship product since it removed the physical home button from the iPhone X in 2017. The iPhone brought in $209.6 billion, or just over half of Apple’s sales, in its most recent fiscal year. Former CEO Tim Cook handed over the leadership baton to Ternus with a video about how to start the presentation that ended with a close-up of Cook, who said, “Not me. That’s your guy,” pointing back toward Ternus. Ternus touted the iPhone as a personal AI hub that focused on privacy, saying that others wanted to collect and store personal data. “Honestly, trust only goes so far when your data is no longer yours to control,” he said. “That’s why Apple Intelligence runs on device whenever it can.” People look at the new foldable iPhone Duo devices on display during Apple’s event at the Steve Jobs Theater in Cupertino, California, the US on September 9, 2026. — Reuters Apple’s Lilian Rincon, who oversees AI products for the iPhone maker and was recruited from Google earlier this year, described an updated Siri assistant that will work with 300,000 apps at release. Executives also showed off the iPhone 18 Pro and the 18 Pro Max handsets that are the latest versions of Apple’s well-known line, which do not fold. Pricing for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max starts at $1,199 and $1,299, up $100 from the starting prices of the 17 Pro and Pro Max. Apple also unveiled a feature aimed at addressing growing concerns over AI-generated and manipulated images. It introduced a new standard it calls “Apple Reference Image” to prove the authenticity of the images taken with the new iPhone 18 Pro cameras and said it will also support the emerging SynthID standard for identifying images that have been created or edited with AI. The Apple Reference Image feature will not be available in the EU or China. The iPhone 18 Pro will also include the new A20 Pro chip, which brings improvements to help advanced AI models to run directly on iPhones. Apple CEO John Ternus speaks as Apple holds an event at the Steve Jobs Theater on its campus in Cupertino, California, the US on September 9, 2026. — Reuters “Apple Intelligence and Siri are front and centre. Apple is using its biggest strength, the sheer scale of its hardware base, to make AI an integral part of the everyday experience across devices,” PP Foresight analyst Paolo Pescatore said. Shares were down about one per cent during the Apple presentation. The company also said a new version of AirPods would start at $129 with noise cancellation, a first for its budget line of earbuds, and that a $149 version will be available with extra features such as wireless charging and on-stem volume control that will allow users to adjust the volume by swiping up or down on the stem. Apple also introduced the Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4, positioning them as major health-focused upgrades. That includes a redesigned sensor system that collects heart rate more frequently than before and powers new features that gauge recovery and fitness. The company said the watches use new Apple silicon and improved sensors to deliver what it called the most accurate heart-rate tracking in a wearable. Premium pricing challenge Ternus previously served as Apple’s hardware chief but has kept a low public profile aside from a handful of product introductions and sustainability initiatives. It will fall to Ternus to persuade Apple’s customers that they need a foldable device that analysts believe could cost more than $2,000, a new high for a global brand that has defined mass luxury. While Samsung Electronics and Huawei Technologies have sold folding phones since 2019, the devices have remained a niche among tech enthusiasts. But even with a steep price tag, analyst firms such as International Data Corporation expect Apple to sell every foldable iPhone it can produce and secure a 40pc share of the lucrative niche by the end of next year. Wednesday’s event is also expected to mark a major change in Apple’s annual product schedule. While analysts expect Apple to show off new watches, they anticipate the company will hold off on updates to its more affordable iPhone models until next spring and instead focus only on the new folding device and its iPhone Pro and Pro Max lineup. The move is aimed at smoothing out Apple’s annual sales cycle, which typically shows a large bump in revenue during the year-end holiday quarter for the US and Europe.

items.title: Le RNI désigne Salma Benaziz comme porte-parole du parti pendant la campagne électorale
items.description: Le Rassemblement national des indépendants (RNI) a annoncé la désignation de Salma Benaziz en qualité de porte-parole officielle du parti durant la campagne électorale, dans le cadre du renforcement de son dispositif de communication institutionnelle et de l’accompagnement des différentes étapes de la campagne et des prochaines échéances électorales. À ce titre, Salma Benaziz sera chargée de la communication officielle du parti avec les médias nationaux et internationaux. Elle aura également pour mission de présenter les positions du RNI, d’expliquer les grandes lignes de son programme électoral et d’interagir avec les questions et sujets liés à la campagne et à son actualité. Cette nomination intervient dans le cadre de la volonté du RNI de mettre en place une communication claire, organisée et responsable avec l’opinion publique, tout en veillant à ce que les positions, engagements et programme du parti soient transmis aux citoyennes et aux citoyens avec précision et transparence. Le parti estime que cette démarche doit contribuer à rehausser le niveau du débat politique et électoral. Le RNI réaffirme, à cette occasion, son ouverture à l’ensemble des médias et sa disposition à interagir avec eux, ainsi qu’à leur fournir les données et éclaircissements relatifs à ses positions, son programme et ses activités durant les différentes phases de la campagne électorale. items.title: Winners of Ocean Photographer of the Year 2026
items.description: © Jenny Stock / Ocean Photographer of the Year Winner, Female Fifty Fathoms Award. An American crocodile moves through the mangroves of Cuba, a habitat that provides shelter for crocodiles feeding, breeding, nesting, and raising their young. © Marc Lenfant / Ocean Photographer of the Year Finalist, Adventure. Three surfers converge on the same wave at Teahupoʻo, French Polynesia, after a paddler is thrown from his board. The tow-in surfer immediately changes course, grabbing the cameraman to avoid a collision. © Julien Anton / Ocean Photographer of the Year Overall Winner, Ocean Photographer of the Year 2026. An adult seahorse pictured with newly born juveniles in the shallow seaweed-filled waters of Moorea, French Polynesia. While it is not known whether these seahorses are related, their arrangement creates the impression of a farewell, as if the tiny seahorses have gathered around their father after he has released them into the world. © Ajiex Dharma / Ocean Photographer of the Year Finalist, Fine Art. A hinge-back cleaning shrimp rests against a pink barrel sponge in Bali, Indonesia; its eyes are sharply focused while the surrounding colors dissolve into a soft blur. © Jenny Stock / Ocean Photographer of the Year Winner, Female Fifty Fathoms Award. A mother humpback whale and her calf glide through Tonga’s warm, sheltered waters. The calf stays close to its mother at first, then becomes curious, swimming in playful circles and approaching the camera. The mother remains calm and watchful, guiding her young when it comes too close. © Romain Barats / Ocean Photographer of the Year Finalist, Conservation Impact. Three gentoo penguins stand beside the rusting remains of the former Hektor whaling station at Whalers Bay, Deception Island, Antarctica. Once a center for Antarctic whaling, the site is now being reclaimed by wildlife and the harsh polar environment. © Lars von Ritter Zahony / Ocean Photographer of the Year Finalist, Adventure. Sunlight pours through cracks in an iceberg in East Greenland, illuminating the seabed like a natural theater. Created by a storm just days earlier, these openings allow light to reach an underwater world usually hidden in darkness. © Allan Cronin / Ocean Photographer of the Year Finalist, Wildlife. A New Zealand fur seal tears apart a rough skate in the waters of New Zealand, while seabirds gather for the scraps. Unable to swallow such large prey whole, the seal throws the skate repeatedly to break it into smaller pieces. © James Ferrara / Ocean Photographer of the Year Second Place, Fine Art. A common octopus reveals its intricate suckers, textured skin, and watchful eye in the waters of Blue Heron Bridge, Florida. Known for its rich marine life, this shallow dive site provided the setting for a close encounter with one of the ocean’s most intelligent animals. © Richard Condlyffe / Ocean Photographer of the Year Finalist, Fine Art. A ladybug amphipod, only 3 millimeters long, rests on a blue sea squirt in the coral reefs of Komodo, Indonesia. © Gergo Rugli / Ocean Photographer of the Year Third Place, Human Connection. A teenager stands at Bronte Ocean Pool, Sydney, as a powerful swell sends waves crashing over the closed bathing site. While the conditions forced beaches to shut, people watched the waves from behind the fence. A group of locals climbed into the closed area and stood on the edge, waiting for the waves to crash over them and sweep them across the pool. c© Thomas Pavy / Ocean Photographer of the Year First Place, Conservation Hope. A great hammerhead shark, known as Tamataroa in French Polynesia, is photographed at 55 meters depth in Tiputa Pass, Rangiroa Atoll, during a population survey. This image represents the moment an anonymous shark becomes a known individual. Through photo identification and laser-calibrated video photogrammetry, scientists can track sharks over time to measure their size, sex, and population trends. © Leighton Lum / Ocean Photographer of the Year Finalist, Conservation Hope. A Hawaiian monk seal rests with her week-old pup on Kaimana Beach in Waikīkī. Mothers nurse their pups for around six weeks without feeding, losing up to a third of their body weight while the pup grows before becoming independent. © Lin Yongxuan / Ocean Photographer of the Year Finalist, Conservation Hope. At sunrise, a traditional fishing village shares the coastline with rows of oﬀshore wind turbines stretching across the sea, on Nanri Island, Fujian, China. © James Ferrara / Ocean Photographer of the Year First Place, Conservation Impact. A whale shark is surrounded by divers and snorkelers in the Maldives, revealing the overwhelming pressure that crowded wildlife tourism can place on marine animals. With almost 50 people visible in the frame, this image captures the reality behind some popular wildlife encounters: an animal seeking space while people compete for a closer view. It challenges us to rethink how we experience and protect the species we admire. © Yuta Shigeno / Ocean Photographer of the Year Third Place, Conservation Hope. A male white-spotted puﬀerfish creates an intricate spawning nest in the sand. The fish carefully shapes a two-meter-wide radial pattern using only his fins. Built over several days, this structure and its subtle details reveal the extraordinary eﬀort this small fish invests in reproduction. © Iris Uijttewaal / Ocean Photographer of the Year Finalist, Ocean Unseen. A pygmy seahorse, no larger than a grain of rice, clings to a delicate hydroid in the reefs of Raja Ampat, Indonesia. Perfectly camouflaged, these tiny animals are rarely seen, even by experienced divers. © Daniel Taylor / Ocean Photographer of the Year Finalist, Conservation Impact. A silky shark circles helplessly after taking bait from an illegal longline, its fate sealed by a steel hook and heavy line designed to prevent escape. Photographed less than 48 hours after Baja California’s seasonal shark-fishing ban ended, the image reveals a hidden reality unfolding far from shore. A small group of pilot fish remains beside the shark, highlighting how the loss of one animal can ripple throughout an entire ecosystem. © Chen Lin / Ocean Photographer of the Year Finalist, Human Connection. From above, moored fishing and tourist boats bloom across the sapphire-blue sea, like the petals of a flower. Fringed by golden coastal vegetation, the shoreline becomes an abstract pattern that is diﬃcult to recognize from ground level. © Mitsuna Kawai / Ocean Photographer of the Year First Place, Ocean Unseen. A ribbonfish rises vertically through the dark waters of Osezaki, Japan. Its long, silver body and delicate fins are adapted for life in the open ocean. This image was captured during a winter blackwater dive. Around the ribbonfish, a swarm of salps—small jelly-like animals that feed on tiny particles in the ocean—provides a glimpse of life moving through the deep sea. © Lana Tannir / Ocean Photographer of the Year Finalist, Conservation Hope. Animal care workers perform daily physiotherapy on Norah, a juvenile harbour porpoise undergoing rehabilitation at SOS Dolfijn in the Netherlands. Rescued after being stranding on the Dutch coast, Norah was treated for multiple serious conditions, including pneumonia and severe muscle spasms. This image captures the intensive care required to return her to the sea. To see all of the winning images, be sure to visit Oceanographic Magazine ’s full gallery .

items.title: Carabao Cup: Chelsea hand 16-year-old Watson debut against Leeds
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Chelsea have handed 16-year-old Reggie Watson his senior debut against Leeds United in Wednesday’s Carabao Cup third-round clash at Stamford Bridge. Manager Xabi Alonso has made nine changes from the side that lost 2-1 to Arsenal on Sunday, with Watson named in the starting XI for the 8pm kick-off. Watson, the son of former Wigan captain Ben Watson, impressed during Chelsea’s pre-season and now makes his first competitive appearance for the Blues. Mike Penders replaces first-choice goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez, while Levi Colwill returns to the defence. Valentin Barco makes his first start for Chelsea, with Pep Chavarría also coming into the side. Estêvão Willian and Jamie Gittens start in attack, while Danny Welbeck leads the line. Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and João Pedro have been rested and are among the substitutes, alongside Reece James, Jorrel Hato and Pedro Neto. Chelsea XI: Mike Penders; Josh Acheampong, Maxence Lacroix, Levi Colwill; Malo Gusto, Reggie Watson, Valentin Barco, Pep Chavarría; Estêvão Willian, Jamie Gittens; Danny Welbeck. Subs: Emiliano Martinez, Wesley Fofana, Jorrel Hato, Reece James, Pedro Neto, Cole Palmer, Geovany Quenda, Morgan Rogers, João Pedro. Meanwhile, Leeds have made eight changes from their 1-1 draw with Brighton, with new signings Michael Zetterer and Melvin Bard making their debuts. Leeds XI: Michael Zetterer; Melvin Bard, James Justin, Tarik Muharemović, Jaka Bijol; Ethan Ampadu, Sean Longstaff; Dan James, Josh Wilson, Brenden Aaronson; Lukas Nmecha. Subs: James Trafford, Junior Firpo, Albert Gudmundsson, Maxence Lacroix, Ao Tanaka, Anton Stach, Noah Okafor, Largie Ramazani, Dominic Calvert-Lewin. Chelsea remain without Moisés Caicedo, Jordan Henderson, Marco Palestra and Emmanuel Emegha, with Alonso previously confirming that Caicedo and Palestra were not ready to return and would not be risked early. Chelsea will be looking to bounce back from their first competitive defeat under Alonso and reach the Carabao Cup fourth round. Leeds, meanwhile, are seeking to continue their unbeaten start to the Premier League season and advance after making eight changes of their own. The match kicks off at 8pm at Stamford Bridge. The post Carabao Cup: Chelsea hand 16-year-old Watson debut against Leeds appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Profanation du drapeau national dans un hôtel à Alger : peines réduites en appel
items.description: Les peines ont été réduites en appel, mais elles restent lourdes. Les auteurs de la profanation de l’emblème national dans un hôtel de la capitale viennent d'être jugés devant la Cour d'appel d’Alger. Le 8 juin dernier, le tribunal de Bir Mourad Rais a condamné à 7 ans de prison ferme et à 500 000 dinars d’amende deux individus filmés trois jours plus tôt en train de piétiner le drapeau national lors d’un événement au Legacy Luxury Hotel, sis à Hydra (Alger). La vidéo, largement partagée sur les réseaux sociaux, avait choqué l’opinion publique. Profanation du drapeau national : 5 ans de prison ferme pour les mis en cause La Cour d’Alger a rendu ce mercredi 9 septembre son verdict dans le procès en appel de cette affaire. Selon le média Ennahar , la dixième chambre pénale de cette juridiction d'appel a réduit les peines prononcées en première instance et condamné les deux mis en cause, Kh.A.A, organisateur de l’événement, et A.M.S, qui a filmé la scène, à cinq ans de prison ferme, assortis du paiement solidaire de la somme de 20 millions de dinars au Trésor public. Parallèlement à ces poursuites judiciaires, le ministère du Tourisme et de l’Artisanat avait procédé, dès la diffusion de la vidéo, à la fermeture immédiate de l'établissement hôtelier, avec retrait de l'autorisation d'exploitation, pour « atteinte aux symboles de l'État et profanation de l’emblème national » . L’article Profanation du drapeau national dans un hôtel à Alger : peines réduites en appel est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Un chef rebelle condamné à 15 ans de prison ferme
items.description: Le chef rebelle centrafricain Abdoulaye Miskine a été condamné, le mercredi 9 septembre 2026, à 15 ans de prison ferme et au versement de 30 millions de F CFA à chacune des familles des victimes par la cour criminelle de N’Djamena. La justice tchadienne l’a reconnu coupable de plusieurs faits graves liés à des exactions commises dans les zones frontalières entre 2002 et 2003. Le verdict est tombé au palais de justice de N’Djamena. Comme le rapportent plusieurs médias, «la cour criminelle du palais de justice de Ndjamena a déclaré le général Miskine coupable d'association de malfaiteurs, de sévices graves, de torture et d'assassinat». De son vrai nom Martin Koumtamadji, Abdoulaye Miskine est l’ancien patron de la garde présidentielle centrafricaine et le dirigeant du Front démocratique du peuple centrafricain (FDPC). Les faits qui lui sont reprochés, notamment des actes de «torture», d’«assassinat» et de «séquestration», remontent à 2002 et 2003 dans des zones situées à la frontière entre le Tchad et la Centrafrique. Ses trois coaccusés ont également été reconnus coupables, mais en qualité de complices. Ils écopent chacun de 10 ans de prison ferme. Le parquet avait requis 30 ans de réclusion contre Abdoulaye Miskine. La défense, qui plaidait l’acquittement, a rejeté le verdict et annoncé son intention de se pourvoir en cassation. Selon l’Agence de Presse Africaine (APA), les avocats contestent la décision et dénoncent un «jugement politique». Arrêté fin 2019 par les forces tchadiennes, Abdoulaye Miskine était depuis détenu à la maison d’arrêt de Klessoum. Avec cette condamnation, la justice tchadienne tourne une nouvelle page dans un dossier qui traînait depuis plus de deux décennies. Mais le verdict est loin de clore l’affaire, la défense ayant annoncé son recours en cassation, laissant désormais la suite de la procédure entre les mains de la juridiction supérieure. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Un chef rebelle condamné à 15 ans de prison ferme est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Only Category C schools available for placement resolution – Northern Region parents say
items.description: Category C is the only option left; that is the reality facing parents and students at the Ghana Education Service (GES) Northern Regional Education Office in Tamale this week, as the resolution window for second-cycle school placements opens with a narrowed list of schools. Students who have issues with their residential status are logging onto the placement portal only to find that Category A and B schools are not available for selection. “Only Category C schools are there for them to make changes on. Category A and B schools are not available. They don’t even appear on it for us to work on them,” Anthony Lansa,h the Northern Regional Examinations Coordinator for GES, told JoyNews . He said what this means is the students have just the category C to select. “It means that they’ve exposed them to only Category C schools so far as this resolution is concerned,” he added. Mr Lansah said the resolution process itself is moving smoothly and his team is attending to parents and candidates. But for some parents, the challenge is more than the categories on offer. Richard Baba Alhassan, a parent who travelled to the regional office, said his child had selected schools within the Tamale Metro, including Dabokpa and Tamale Senior High School, but was placed at Zugu Dabogni Technical Institute in Kumbungu, which he said was never among their eight choices. “That one was not part of our request,” he said. He said his son scored an aggregate 23. “My child is supposed to be in Category A school, now they have moved him to Category C,” Mr Alhassan added. He said he came with three copies of the choice list submitted through his child’s junior high school to prove the assigned school was not selected, but officials told him the system showed it was his choice. Another parent, Asmawu Sulemana, said she first went to the regional office on Monday to correct her child’s placement but was told to return later. She returned on Tuesday, wrote her complaint and waited her turn, only to be told her case could not be handled in Tamale. She was told she would have to go to Accra because the school she chose is not in the Northern Region. Mrs Sulemana said they told her there is a school with a similar name in the Northern Region; she had chosen the one outside the region; and for that reason, the Northern Region centre could not process her complaint.
