items.title: 59,300 students receive GH¢210m in enhanced student loans – SLTF
items.description: The Student Loan Trust Fund (SLTF) says it has disbursed GH¢210 million in enhanced student loans to 59,300 tertiary students this year. The Chief Executive Officer of the SLTF, Dr Saajida Shiraz, said the intervention forms part of government’s efforts to ensure that financial constraints do not prevent students from accessing tertiary education. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Wednesday, September 9, Dr Shiraz said the Fund has been able to meet all demands for student loans this year, following increased government prioritisation of student financial support. “This year alone, we did about 59,300 to be exact, and we disbursed GH¢210 million in student loans,” she said. She said, in addition to the traditional and enhanced student loans, the Fund has also expanded support under the Student Loan Plus initiative. According to her, 1,997 students benefited from the initiative, including 626 students enrolled at the Ghana School of Law. She explained that the expansion followed a directive from President John Mahama to extend student loan support to persons pursuing professional legal education. Dr Shiraz said that about GH¢20 million was spent to pay the fees of the 626 Ghana School of Law students directly to their institution. She added that “the Fund has also spent GH¢10 million so far to support tertiary students with disabilities, covering tuition and residential payments.” The SLTF CEO said government is, however, working on the policy framework for additional support, including stipends and assistive learning devices for students with disabilities.

items.title: Trump gave $45,000 cash gifts to close aide Natalie Harp and others
items.description: President Donald Trump gave tens of ​thousands of dollars in cash gifts last year to executive assistant Natalie Harp and three other ‌close aides working in the West Wing, according to financial disclosures released by the White House. The payments raised ethics concerns because federal employees are generally barred by statute from receiving compensation beyond their government salaries. Harp, communications adviser Margo Martin and deputy director of Oval ​Office operations Chamberlain Harris each received $45,000, described in their disclosures as “Cash Gift for Holidays.” The payments were equivalent ​to roughly one-third of the aides’ federal salaries of $150,000 per year, according to the White ⁠House annual personnel report to Congress. Walt Nauta, another aide who works as the director of Oval Office ​operations, received $20,000 in cash, the disclosures show. His annual compensation is $175,000. The Washington Post first reported the gifts on Tuesday. “A White ​House staffer is not your Fifth Avenue doorman,” Richard W. Painter, a law professor who served as the chief White House ethics lawyer between 2005 and 2007 under President George W. Bush, said in a social media post. GIFTS COMPLY WITH RULES: WHITE HOUSE White House ​spokesman Davis Ingle said the gifts complied with ethics rules. “The President has a longstanding practice of giving Christmas ​gifts to people in his orbit, including at times employees and aides, both in government and in his time in the private ‌sector,” ⁠Ingle said in a statement on Wednesday. “The gifts at issue here have nothing to do with any of these individuals’ official government duties, and therefore are entirely permissible under relevant legal and ethical standards.” Harp and Nauta are among Trump’s most trusted aides, with near-constant access to the president during long days on the road or at the White ​House. Harp drew public scrutiny last ​month when the Washington ⁠Post reported that she and Nauta were in a catering truck that secretly moved Trump to a flight he took in July from Turkey to the United Kingdom amid concerns ​about potential threats from Iran. Harp exercises control over Trump’s Truth Social account, posting on ​his behalf ⁠and helping draft social media statements, according to a person familiar with her role. Colleagues sometimes call her the “human printer” as she provides often favorable news coverage to Trump from a portable printer that she carries. Nauta, a former White House ⁠valet, faced ​accusations from federal prosecutors of helping Trump hide top-secret documents that the ​Republican president took when he completed his first term at the White House in 2021. Nauta pleaded not guilty, and the case was dropped ​after Trump returned to office.

items.title: El Jadida accueille la 5e édition du Grand Prix d’Afrique
items.description: Après Marrakech et Casablanca, le Grand Prix d’Afrique pose pour la première fois ses valises à El Jadida. Du 10 au 12 septembre 2026, la SOREC et l’Association des Loteries d’Afrique réuniront les principaux acteurs du secteur autour des nouvelles tendances de consommation et des transformations des marchés africains. Le Grand Prix d’Afrique poursuit son développement au Maroc. Pour sa 5e édition, l’événement s’installe pour la première fois à El Jadida, après trois rendez-vous organisés à Marrakech et une précédente édition à Casablanca en 2025. Organisée par la Société Royale d’Encouragement du Cheval (SOREC) et l’Association des Loteries d’Afrique (ALA), cette nouvelle édition réunira, pendant trois jours, acteurs des jeux et des loteries, professionnels des courses hippiques, experts et partenaires internationaux. Au-delà de la compétition hippique, le Grand Prix d’Afrique s’est progressivement imposé comme une plateforme de rencontres et d’échanges autour des évolutions du secteur sur le continent. Les rencontres professionnelles débuteront jeudi 10 septembre au Parc d’Exposition Mohammed VI, avec l’inauguration officielle et l’ouverture de l’exposition B2B. Celle-ci réunira 25 partenaires, exposants et startups, venus présenter leurs solutions, innovations et expertises dédiées au secteur. Le temps fort de cette édition est prévu vendredi 11 septembre avec le séminaire de l’ALA, placé sous le thème : « Cultures, comportements sociaux et consommation dans le business des loteries africaines ». Experts, représentants des loteries africaines et partenaires internationaux échangeront autour de l’influence des spécificités socioculturelles sur les comportements des consommateurs. Les discussions porteront notamment sur les caractéristiques propres aux différents marchés locaux, l’évolution des habitudes de consommation et les nouvelles attentes des publics. L’objectif sera également d’identifier des pistes permettant aux opérateurs d’adapter leurs offres et leurs stratégies aux réalités de chaque marché africain. La SOREC et l’ALA misent sur la coopération Pour Omar Skalli, directeur général de la SOREC, cette cinquième édition constitue une nouvelle étape dans le développement de l’événement. Son installation à El Jadida traduit, selon lui, la volonté de renforcer le rayonnement du Grand Prix d’Afrique et d’offrir aux acteurs du continent un rendez-vous à la hauteur de leurs ambitions. De son côté, Dramane Coulibaly, président de l’ALA, souligne la dynamique du partenariat entre les deux organisations et leur volonté de renforcer la coopération entre les loteries africaines. Le choix du thème consacré aux comportements et aux modes de consommation doit notamment permettre de mieux comprendre les mutations à l’œuvre sur les marchés africains et d’accompagner les évolutions du secteur. Après deux journées placées sous le signe des échanges, de l’expertise et de la réflexion stratégique, le samedi 12 septembre sera consacré à la compétition hippique, venant clôturer cette cinquième édition du Grand Prix d’Afrique. Avec cette nouvelle étape à El Jadida, l’événement confirme ainsi sa vocation à rapprocher les professionnels africains et internationaux autour des transformations d’un secteur en pleine évolution, tout en associant réflexion stratégique et passion des courses hippiques. The post El Jadida accueille la 5e édition du Grand Prix d’Afrique appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Why Israel Reacted With Fury to U.K. Sanctions on West Bank Settlements
Pakistan among Arab, Muslim nations welcoming UK ban on imports from illegal Israeli settlements
items.description: Pakistan, along with seven other Arab and Muslim countries, on Wednesday welcomed the United Kingdom’s decision to ban imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. UK imposed the trade measures on Tuesday, alongside Canada and France. The decision was announced by British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, who accused the Israeli government of turning a “blind eye” to what he called “ethnic cleansing” by settlers in the West Bank. Meanwhile, a joint statement by the foreign ministers of 12 nations, including Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain and Sweden, also expressed an intention to follow suit and stressed that the Israeli government’s actions in the West Bank undermined the possibility of a two-state solution. A joint statement by the foreign ministers of Pakistan, Turkiye, Egypt, Indonesia, Jordan, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, issued by the Foreign Office (FO), expressed hope that the international community would take similar action in accordance with international law and “hold accountable settlement organisations and individuals engaged in illegal settlement activities”. The ministers also welcomed an earlier joint statement on the two-state solution issued by the foreign ministers of Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain, Sweden and the United Kingdom. “They encourage the international community to build on these steps and adopt concrete measures to bring an end to activities that support or sustain illegal Israeli settlements in the Occupied Palestinian Territory,” the FO stated. It added that the eight countries considered the ban to be in line with international law and relevant United Nations resolutions, including Security Council Resolution 2334 (2016). They also viewed the decision as consistent with the International Court of Justice’s July 19, 2024, advisory opinion, which requires states “not to recognise as legal the situation arising from Israel’s unlawful occupation and not to render aid or assistance in maintaining the situation created by Israel’s occupation”. “In this regard, they reiterate their call for Israel to rescind all measures taken in connection with settlement activities and other measures aimed at altering the geographic and demographic character of the Occupied Palestinian Territory,” the joint statement read. The joint statement also stressed that Gaza is an integral part of Palestine and called for the “full and immediate” implementation of US President Donald Trump’s ‘Comprehensive Plan to End the Gaza Conflict’. The ministers reiterated that the only viable path to a lasting and comprehensive peace was the implementation of a two-state solution and the establishment of an independent, sovereign, contiguous and viable Palestinian state based on the June 4, 1967, borders, with Jerusalem as its capital, in accordance with international law. Islamabad stands by Palestine Earlier today, Pakistan welcomed the United Kingdom-led decision to impose trade sanctions on Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, saying that the illegal settlements undermined efforts towards a two-state solution, a separate statement from the FO read. In a statement on its X account, the FO welcomed the decision and said: “The continued expansion of illegal settlements in the occupied Palestinian territory constitutes a blatant violation of international law as well as relevant UN Security Council resolutions.” Maintaining that Israel’s actions were a hindrance to a two-state solution, the FO also welcomed the joint statement by the 12 countries, which it said were considering “similar measures and support[ing] such efforts against the illegal Israeli settlements”. “Pakistan hopes that these measures will send a clear and unequivocal message of rejection of illegal actions in the occupied Palestinian territory,” the statement said. Islamabad reiterated support for Palestine, vowing to stand by its people and “their just struggle for self-determination”. In response to the UK’s actions, Israel ordered the closure of the UK’s consulate in Jerusalem earlier today. It also said it would expel British representatives at a centre monitoring the US-brokered ceasefire plan in Gaza, bar British training for Palestinian Authority forces and ban 12 Britons, mostly members of parliament, from visiting the country. Miliband, in response, condemned Israel’s actions as “regrettable and damaging”. Speaking to BBC Radio , he also rejected suggestions that the sanctions would impact intelligence cooperation with Israel. “We have important intelligence and security relationships with Israel, and I’m confident they will continue,” he said, declining to go into details. “And I was very clear yesterday that we do believe in working with our Israeli partners when it comes to the threats they face from Iran,” he added.

items.description: L’euro semble avoir trouvé sa place sur le marché noir des devises en Algérie. Après les montagnes russes que ses cours ont connues en 2025, il affiche une relative stabilité en cette année 2026, tout en restant à un niveau élevé. En novembre 2025, la monnaie unique européenne a enregistré son plus haut record, qui n’a jamais été égalé depuis, à 292 dinars algériens l’unité. Mais après avoir frôlé le seuil des 300 dinars, l’euro a reculé, perdant jusqu’à 15 dinars en l’espace d’un mois, avant de s’installer à la fin du mois de décembre sous la barre des 280 dinars algériens (277,50 DZD pour un euro le 31 décembre 2025). Marché noir des devises : un euro sous les 280 et un dollar sous les 240 dinars Malgré quelques fluctuations, l’euro n’a pas trop bougé depuis le début de l’année 2026. Les cambistes du Square Port-Saïd le proposent ce mercredi 9 septembre à 276 dinars l’unité, soit le même taux de change que celui proposé en début de semaine (dimanche 6 septembre). Même en comparaison avec ses cours du mois d'août, l’euro montre des signes de stagnation. La monnaie unique européenne était déjà cotée à 276 dinars l’unité au début du mois précédent, et autour des 277 dinars en juin et en juillet. Même si l’on remonte au premier semestre, l'euro dépasse rarement la barre des 280 dinars. Cette stagnation de l’euro sur le marché noir des devises peut être le fruit des mesures prises par le gouvernement, notamment l’interdiction de l’importation groupée des voitures de moins de trois ans de Chine, mais aussi le plafonnement du montant à exporter par année civile à 7.500 €. Elle peut être liée aux mesures prises dans le cadre du blanchiment d’argent qui a fortement réduit l’utilisation du cash. La stagnation a aussi touché le dollar américain. Le billet vert s’échange chez les cambistes du Square ce mercredi contre 237,50 dinars algériens, soit une hausse de seulement 0,50 dinars algériens par rapport à dimanche dernier. Pour rappel, le dollar était déjà sous la barre des 240 dinars à la mi-août dernier. Dans sa cotation commerciale d’ouverture du dinar algérien de ce mercredi 9 septembre, la Banque d’Algérie affiche un euro coté à 154,64 dinars à la vente contre 154,69 DZD la veille et un dollar coté à 133,05 dinars contre 133,02 hier mardi. L’article Dinar algérien : l’euro et le dollar stagnent à des niveaux élevés est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Sommet «international» sur l’espace à Paris : un échec annoncé ?
items.description: Emmanuel Macron reve de reunir a Paris les grands acteurs du spatial pour dessiner les contours d'une Europe enfin maîtresse de son destin orbital. Le Sommet international sur l'espace, qui s'ouvre ce 9 septembre pour deux jours au Grand Palais, risque pourtant de rappeler que, dans l'espace comme sur Terre, l'Europe peine encore a jouer dans la meme categorie que les etats-Unis. L'occasion pour le president francais, qui s'est rendu sur place, d'annoncer que « plus de 50 projets vont etre signes », des « projets entre la France et l'Allemagne » ainsi qu'avec « les emirats arabes unis », a-t-il notamment precise lors d'une prise de parole devant une assemblee quelque peu… clairsemee . La veille, un accord d'un milliard d'euros entre la societe emiratie Marlan Space et les Francais Loft Orbital et Mistral avait ete annonce, en vue de deployer la premiere constellation satellite consacree a l'IA. Reste a savoir si la France est en mesure de « rattraper son retard » en matiere de course a l'espace. « Cela va etre un peu complique », a concede ce 9 septembre sur France info Marie-Ange Sanguy, redactrice en chef du magazine Espace et Exploration, avant d'estimer que – hormis sur de petits lanceurs – les Francais sont « obliges de penser europeen ». D'autres y croient davantage, a l'instar du president de la Region Normandie, Herve Morin, qui avec une pointe d'humour, lancait le 4 septembre a Elon Musk « qu'il a interet a bien se tenir », a l'occasion de l'inauguration a Vernon d'une usine de fusees reutilisables d'une filiale d'ArianeGroup. Spatial : des acteurs majeurs qui brillent par leur absence a Paris Le president francais avait pourtant vu grand. Presente comme un rendez-vous destine a faire emerger une « vision politique commune » et a renforcer la souverainete europeenne dans le spatial, le sommet doit reunir quelque « 2 000 participants » selon l'elysee . Sommet auquel ont ete, rappelle la presse francaise, « convies 120 pays sauf la Russie, l'Iran et la Coree du Nord ». Des exclus d'office – dont l'une des grandes puissances spatiales historiques – auxquels s'ajoutent… ceux qui ont decline l'invitation, au premier rang desquels des geants americains du domaine. Parmi les acteurs etats-uniens qui ne participeront pas a ce « sommet » voulu par Emmanuel Macron, figurent SpaceX et Blue Origin. La presse francaise parle d'« absence », reprenant les rumeurs selon lesquelles Donald Trump serait a la manœuvre. Tout aussi genant, Friedrich Merz a qui « Macron avait offert la copresidence » du sommet « finalement ne peut pas venir », a souligne un journaliste sur France info, avant de rappeler le « chacun pour soi » lance par les Allemands en matiere de course a l'espace. En effet, alors que la France s'entete dans la voie d'une cooperation avec l'Allemagne quitte a donner a Ariane 6 des airs de SCAF, la societe allemande Isar Aerospace a place en orbite basse le 5 septembre sa fusee Spectrum, tiree depuis la Norvege. Une premiere en Europe continentale.

items.title: Urgent-Acccident de la route à Kagbélén: un camion percute une moto et fait deux morts
items.description: Un accident mortel de la circulation s’est produit ce mercredi 9 septembre 2026, aux environs de 16 heures, sur la route nationale 2 (RN2), à Kagbélén-Village, dans la commune urbaine de Kagbélén. Le drame, survenu à proximité d’une mosquée, a fait deux morts. Selon les témoignages recueillis sur place, l’accident a impliqué une moto transportant deux personnes, dont une femme, et un camion. Présent sur les lieux au moment des faits, le chef du secteur de Kagbélén Village-Mosquée a relaté les circonstances de l’accident : « nous étions assis au bord de la route. Un motard arrivait avec une dame assise derrière lui. Au même moment, le camion était en train de passer. C’est le deuxième pneu du camion qui a rattrapé la moto. Ils sont tombés sur place. » D’après ce témoignage, le camion aurait percuté la moto alors qu’il effectuait une manœuvre de dépassement. Sous la violence du choc, les deux occupants de la moto ont été projetés au sol et ont succombé à leurs blessures sur place. Les circonstances exactes de l’accident restent toutefois à déterminer. Après le drame, les corps des deux victimes ont été transportés à l’hôpital préfectoral de Dubréka pour les formalités d’usage. Cet accident relance une nouvelle fois la question de la sécurité routière sur cet axe très fréquenté, marqué par une forte cohabitation entre motocyclistes, véhicules de transport et poids lourds.

items.title: The Inside Story of What Happened at Stars and Stripes
items.description: A “chicken plate,” in military parlance, is a protective shield used in a variety of combat situations. During the Vietnam War, chicken plates were inserted into vests—they are resistant against small-arms fire, but they’re also bulky and hot. So some pilots sat on them instead, which had the added benefit of providing protection against bullets that came from below. I first encountered another type of chicken plate in Iraq, where I was embedded with a convoy of American service members patrolling outside of Tikrit. On this particular morning, I sat alongside three soldiers inside an up-armored Humvee while a gunner manned the turret. But that gunner—James Murphy, a sergeant from New Jersey—wasn’t sitting in his sling, which was little more than a seat-belt strap hooked between two sides of the turret. If he sat down, the chicken plate would block his view. This left Murphy with a choice: stand up for hours and expose his head and chest, or remain behind the plate’s limited protection and endanger the convoy by missing a threat. For the dozen or so gunners I spoke with, the choice was clear. Two of them removed the chicken plate entirely for a better view. The military had no specific data on gunner casualties or whether the chicken plates were preventing them. Yet an Army general in Iraq was asking his staff why they were losing so many gunners. One officer I spoke with at the time told me that the answer was obvious the moment someone stood in the turret. [ Tom Nichols: Hegseth’s Pentagon lurches off the rails ] I reported a series of stories on gunners for Stars and Stripes , a newspaper with a long history of editorial independence despite being housed within the Department of Defense. A few weeks later, after returning to my home at the time—a room at the bachelor officers’ quarters on a Marine Corps base in Okinawa—I received a message from our Pentagon beat reporter, who told me that military officials had read the series and were fast-tracking improved equipment for deployment. They’d found a way to help protect the gunners without blocking their view from the turret. I don’t want to overstate my role. At least some military officials were aware of the issue and had been testing prototypes for better shields. But many of the soldiers weren’t willing to discuss with senior leaders the specifics of what they needed, out of concern that they’d be viewed as complaining. I’m grateful that they trusted me enough to tell their stories. Looking back now, what feels remarkable isn’t the lack of proper equipment. It’s the way the Pentagon was willing to take independent journalism that spotlighted deficiencies and use it to improve conditions for service members. Uniformed military leaders have not lost the means to analyze and act on useful journalism. But publicly denouncing the reporting or the news outlet makes it far less likely that they will. Attacking people for telling the truth creates a chilling effect for truth tellers—including those who are themselves in the military. The best journalism unearths information that complex bureaucracies overlook or suppress, intentionally or not. When leaders treat asking tough questions and reporting uncomfortable facts as disloyalty, they devalue a tool that can help them fix crucial problems. The danger in this devaluation is immense, especially now; it comes as U.S. service members are once again fighting in the Middle East. The Pentagon hasn’t held a press briefing on combat operations in Iran since May 5. The Correspondents’ Corridor, where reporters worked inside the Pentagon for decades, is closed while court appeals continue on press-access restrictions. The New York Times is suing the Pentagon on First Amendment grounds, arguing that the Pentagon’s attempts to prevent independent reporting are clearly unconstitutional. (I should disclose that I, too, am suing the Pentagon. I was fired after I said in an appearance on CBS News that my personal red line would be if the Pentagon ever instructed me not to publish a perfectly accurate story. It is telling that I am being fired for describing the most anodyne of journalistic ethics, a position that any self-respecting reporter in any free society would hold, and that the Pentagon interpreted as insubordination.) Stars and Stripes has its roots in the Civil War, when Union soldiers took over a printing press in Bloomfield, Missouri. The paper was revived during World War I under General John “Black Jack” Pershing and has published continuously since 1942, when General George C. Marshall recognized the value it provided troops and aimed to follow Pershing’s example. “No official control was ever exercised over the matter which went into” Stars and Stripes , Marshall said of the WWI edition . It didn’t take long for that editorial freedom to be challenged. General George Patton complained about the “Willie and Joe” cartoonist Bill Mauldin’s depictions of soldiers as they often appeared—tired and dirty. (Mauldin would have known; he was himself a soldier.) But General Dwight Eisenhower rejected Patton’s drive to control the reporting itself. “It is the soldier’s paper,” he said, “and we won’t interfere,” according to the historian Stephen Ambrose’s foreword in a book by Mauldin, whose wartime cartoons earned him the 1945 Pulitzer Prize. The newspaper continued to operate overseas after World War II, hiring civilian journalists to work alongside service members. But attempts at curtailing Stripes ’ independence periodically arose. Congress documented occasional pressures in the 1960s. In the ’80s, a General Accounting Office report to Congress found conclusive evidence of censorship, and pointed out the “inherent cultural conflict” between the First Amendment mission and the military’s own. Those findings led the House Armed Services Committee to direct the Pentagon to establish an ombudsman, responsible to Congress, who would monitor the free flow of information to service members through Stars and Stripes . And in 1993, a Defense Department directive affirmed that Stars and Stripes is editorially independent of the military chain of command. A subsequent federal regulation added to those protections. In 2020, the Pentagon proposed cutting all funding to Stars and Stripes , after the department’s comptroller stated that it is “probably not the best way that we communicate any longer.” The idea drew a bipartisan rebuke in Congress. The White House agreed with the lawmakers, and Stripes lived on. Last November, I moved to Washington, D.C., to accept the editor-in-chief job at the paper, where I’d already been serving as Europe and Middle East chief, based near Ramstein Air Base, in Germany. Two months later, the Pentagon chief spokesman Sean Parnell fired a broadside at Stars and Stripes . On January 15, he posted on X that the news organization must be rid of “woke distractions that syphon morale.” The same day, the Pentagon revoked the federal regulation it had established in 1994, calling it unnecessary. The Daily Wire , which reported that half of all Stripes content would come from the military’s public-affairs team, and that civilian reporters would be replaced by military members. When Stars and Stripes reporters called the Pentagon press office for comment and clarification, they received nothing more than a referral to the tweet and the Daily Wire story. [ Read: Why is the Pentagon afraid of the press? ] On February 28, the United States and Israel attacked Iran, killing Iranian Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. The first Stars and Stripes story came from a wire service, because there aren’t any Stripes reporters inside Iran. But within hours, we had half a dozen stories focused on the U.S. military bases in the region and the people there. In Bahrain, civilians were given the order to evacuate an hour after missiles began falling on the headquarters base of the U.S. Fifth Fleet. The coverage drew millions of readers, and a video shot by one of our active-duty reporters of a plume rising over the Navy base was viewed all over the world. We worked hard on covering the Iran conflict and thought little of that January tweet—that is, until a Pentagon memo came in mid-March. The memo simultaneously affirmed our independence and added restrictions. That wire-service story from Iran was now forbidden, along with any other paid wire-service news. So were the comics, of all things. Our publishing decisions would be subject to “good order and discipline”—a line borrowed from the Uniform Code of Military Justice. Our military reporters, who function as interns and receive mentorship from seasoned civilian journalists, now had to wonder whether writing a story might land them in legal jeopardy. I told military reporters who were worried that a story might hurt their career to let us know, and we’d reassign it. Meanwhile, the staff never compromised on their ethics and values. They reported fairly and accurately and, when called for, held power to account. The ombudsman wrote a column that assailed the news restrictions, in keeping with the duties set by Congress. Two weeks later, the Defense Department fired her. By the time I sat down with CBS’s David Martin in late June, I had spoken with no fewer than 16 news outlets and authors about Stars and Stripes . Martin asked me about the “woke distractions” referenced in the January tweet and I answered honestly—that the Pentagon had never explained to us what that meant. Martin also asked whether I had a personal red line when it came to press restrictions, and I said that I did. If the Pentagon were to say, “ Don’t run a perfectly accurate story . Run this instead . Here it is, written by the Pentagon . That would be a red line.” My response to hypothetical censorship was consistent with what military leaders have said for more than a century, and with the Defense Department’s own directive barring censorship and news management. It is also consistent with basic journalistic ethics: Without editorial independence, journalists cannot uphold their duty to the public. As part of the CBS interview, the Middle East correspondent Lara Korte stated that she worked for Stars and Stripes , not the Pentagon. She made the distinction to underscore her independence, which is essential to credibility. I learned approximately a week later that the Pentagon press office wasn’t happy about the interview, but that was all I heard. On August 12, seven weeks after the CBS interview, the Pentagon sent notices of proposed separation for Korte and me to Stripes ’ publisher, Max Lederer, and told him to sign them. Lederer was an Airborne soldier turned Army attorney who was awarded the Bronze Star before he joined Stars and Stripes . He worked his way up through business operations to serve for two decades as publisher. He reviewed the separation notices and pointed out legal and ethical inconsistencies. Those concerns were dismissed. Rather than sign the notices, he submitted his resignation. (They fired him instead.) On August 21, the three of us received the separation notices, which listed insubordination as the primary charge. The notices issued to Korte and me cited our CBS comments but didn’t state which order we were purportedly disobeying. Lederer’s firing was for not signing the documents in the first place. That same day, the Pentagon replaced the directive issued in 1993. Among other things, it bars comics deemed editorial in nature and prevents reporters from using the Freedom of Information Act on behalf of the news organization. I can’t think of another American media outlet with the same restriction. [ Anne Applebaum: The Pentagon’s preferred propaganda model ] About an hour after we received our separation notices, the military deputy to the publisher, who’d arrived two weeks earlier, ordered a 10-page document to be published on Stripes.com within 30 minutes. The document stated that Stripes would continue to run independent journalism and that “it is time to take them at their word,” referring to the Pentagon. I do take them at their word. All of the words they’ve put out since January, along with their actions. The Pentagon has articulated a remarkably narrow view of press freedom. The government may stop short of censoring an individual story. But it will seek to fire newsroom leaders for opposing the replacement of accurate reporting with press releases. It will strip an organization of basic reporting tools it deems unnecessary or distasteful. And it will discredit the source of the reporting if a story is perceived as unflattering to the president or his secretary of defense. The press isn’t a perfect institution. A global 2026 Reuters Institute survey found that the percentage of people who report trusting the news dropped to the lowest level since Reuters began asking the question in 2015; in the U.S., only 25 percent of Americans said that they trust the news most of the time. Whatever combination of press failures and partisanship produced this decline, public trust has eroded. And it’s that erosion that has made it much easier for officials to delegitimize accurate, balanced journalism. Reporters, like anyone, make mistakes, but ethical journalism remains fundamentally useful to government and to the citizens who hold it accountable. People in large organizations—the U.S. military included—often avoid delivering bad news for fear of appearing to oppose a leader’s plans. Independent reporting moves information forward, but only if sources know they’ll be able to speak with journalists without fear of reprisal, and if they believe that leaders are open to reacting to criticism like professionals. That’s what happened in Iraq. The gunners knew what they needed to do their job safely. They didn’t want to be viewed as complainers. Independent journalism sent the message to those who needed to hear it. *Image sources: Jim Watson / AFP / Getty; Win McNamee / Getty; Lyalya Go / Getty; HUM Images / Getty; Toronto Star Archives / Getty; Universal History Archive / Getty; Library of Congress.

items.title: Beauty Kabukie Apedoe appointed CEO of Inter Tourism Expo Accra
items.description: The Management Board of Inter Tourism Expo Accra (INTTA) has appointed Beauty Kabukie Apedoe as the organisation’s new Chief Executive Officer. Her appointment forms part of INTTA’s efforts to strengthen its corporate governance and expand its role in promoting tourism, investment, trade, business events and sustainable economic development. Ms Apedoe brings experience in tourism and hospitality management, public relations, strategic communications, events, entrepreneurship, programme management, sustainability advocacy and stakeholder engagement. She holds a bachelor’s degree in Hospitality and Tourism Management from the Ghana Institute of Management and Public Administration (GIMPA), where she was named the best graduating student of the 2023 class at the university’s 23rd congregation. She is also pursuing a Bachelor of Laws degree, with an interest in international trade, business and commercial law. Ms Apedoe previously gained professional experience at the Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA), particularly in public relations, institutional communication and stakeholder engagement. She has also developed expertise in public speaking, content development, corporate communications, event communication and relationship management. INTTA said her understanding of the Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions (MICE) sector would support its ambition to position the Expo as a platform for business partnerships, investment promotion and tourism development. Under her leadership, the organisation is expected to deepen collaboration among tourism operators, government institutions, investors, private-sector organisations, development partners and international stakeholders. Ms Apedoe also brings entrepreneurial experience spanning the events, hospitality, food and agriculture sectors. According to INTTA, this cross-sector experience will support its efforts to connect tourism with agribusiness, trade, investment, infrastructure, digital transformation and sustainable development. Her mandate includes strengthening the organisation’s visibility, expanding strategic partnerships, deepening engagement with tourism businesses and supporting relations with investors and international partners. She is also expected to promote an inclusive approach to tourism development, with particular attention to opportunities for young people, entrepreneurs and emerging businesses. Ms Apedoe has participated in environmental advocacy initiatives, including campaigns on reducing single-use plastics and promoting environmental education. The organisation said her sustainability experience aligns with its commitment to responsible tourism, environmental protection and inclusive economic growth. Chairman of Inter Tourism Expo Accra, Emmanuel Treku, congratulated Ms Apedoe and expressed confidence in her ability to lead the organisation into its next phase. He said her academic achievements, tourism expertise, communications experience, entrepreneurial background, legal studies and commitment to sustainability provided a strong foundation for the role. Mr Treku pledged his full support for her administration and stressed the need for a strong management team and robust corporate governance framework to guide INTTA’s growth. He said the organisation’s future would depend on visionary leadership, professionalism, accountability, strategic partnerships and measurable outcomes. INTTA expressed confidence that Ms Apedoe’s leadership would strengthen its institutional development and advance its objective of using tourism, MICE, trade and investment to promote job creation, enterprise development and sustainable economic growth.

items.title: FATF warns of emerging risks to economies from rising online gaming, gambling operations
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) has warned of emerging risks to economies from rising online gaming and gambling operations, while sharing new risk indicators with countries to combat money laundering and terror financing. “As gaming and gambling services become increasingly digital, cross-border and interconnected, new money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing risks are emerging,” said the FATF, the Paris-based global watchdog on money laundering, terror financing and proliferation financing related to weapons of mass destruction, on Wednesday after conducting surveys across 80 jurisdictions. The findings and risk indicators examine risks across casinos, gambling and online gaming, including online platforms, payment channels, illegal operators and their links to the broader financial system. The FATF said it also sets international standards to combat illicit finance and assesses whether countries are taking effective action. The latest report said the gaming and gambling industries had changed significantly in recent years and continued to evolve through the expansion of online, cross-border, multi-product and multi-payment platforms. “Gaming and gambling establishments and platforms are now part of a broader interconnected value transfer ecosystem with numerous actors, some of which fall outside national anti-money laundering/counter-terrorist financing (AML/CFT) regulatory frameworks,” it said. These factors, as well as the varying scope among jurisdictions in AML/CFT regulation of gambling and understanding of gaming risk-exposed activity, have led to developments in the money laundering (ML), terrorist financing (TF) and, to a somewhat lesser extent, proliferation financing (PF) risks associated with the sector. The FATF also alerted countries and regulators to ways of spotting and blocking the abuse of the gaming and gambling sectors, including criminals using gambling platforms to move money without actually gambling, making multiple small transactions (“smurfing”) to avoid detection, and placing unusually large or coordinated bets on events flagged for possible competition manipulation. Analysis by the FATF identified new opportunities for criminal abuse in the gaming and gambling sectors, following an increase in the global market size, a rise in the use of online platforms and the growing use of payment methods that allow rapid, anonymous transactions across borders. It identified illegal gambling as one of the sector’s most significant risks. In many jurisdictions, illegal markets rival or even exceed the size of legal gambling markets. Illegal gambling operators are prevalent across jurisdictions, regardless of the legal status of gambling or the regulatory frameworks in place. Illegal and unlicensed offshore operators often present themselves as legitimate businesses while offering anonymity and incentives that can attract both consumers and criminal actors. It said technological innovation had expanded activity across online, cross-border and multi-payment platforms, creating increasingly complex ecosystems for regulators and law enforcement. With gaming and gambling activities increasingly interconnected with the wider digital economy, the sector provides multiple points of access to the formal financial system through cash, e-wallets, mobile money and virtual assets. Gaming and gambling platforms depend on a wide range of related services, including social media platforms, digital marketplaces and software developers. These actors may fall outside existing regulatory frameworks, creating additional opportunities for criminal abuse. It warned that criminals and illegal operators can exploit differences in regulatory approaches across jurisdictions. These differences can also create barriers to information sharing between the private and public sectors and pose challenges to international cooperation. The FATF also warned that beneficial ownership and shareholding structures of platforms can be designed to bypass thresholds for regulatory checks, especially when AML/CFT controls and anti-corruption frameworks are weak. FATF President Giles Thomson urged governments to take note of the risk indicators and put in place appropriate risk-based responses — from strengthening oversight and cracking down on illegal and offshore operators to boosting international cooperation and deepening public-private collaboration. It also highlighted the continued threat of criminal infiltration and exploitation of gaming and gambling operators and identified links between gaming and gambling abuse and a range of other offences, including corruption, cyber-enabled fraud, professional money laundering networks, and the use of illegal or unlicensed offshore operators to facilitate criminal activity. The new risk indicators also provide practical guidance to identify, assess and respond to suspicious activity. The indicators highlight behavioural, transactional and operational warning signs associated with money laundering and terrorist financing. These include the use of multiple accounts and payment methods under different identities, discrepancies between customer and payment information, suspicious identity documents and criminal links involving gambling operators or beneficial owners, including involvement in cyber-enabled fraud and organised crime; suspicious betting and transaction patterns; and complex ownership structures that obscure beneficial ownership. Regulators have been alerted to be vigilant for attempts to influence or bribe venue staff through frequent dealings with one or two staff members, requests for cash-ups, claims through lottery tickets, betting slips, vouchers or prize coupons, and taking instructions from customers over a mobile phone. Warning signs also include deliberate attempts to conceal identity, such as repeated use of virtual private networks (VPNs), use of multiple devices and discrepancies between a customer’s claimed residence and their detected location. Customers may also try to open multiple accounts under the same name or a false name, while an internet protocol (IP) address may not match the customer’s stated location.

items.title: Gouvernement Al Amine : Une feuille de route sans détour
items.description: À travers un discours direct, parfois sans détour, le chef du gouvernement s’est ainsi adressé à la représentation nationale, dans le cadre de sa Déclaration de Politique Générale (DPG). De son intervention se dégageait à la fois la rigueur du technicien, la lucidité de l’économiste et la maîtrise d’un homme rompu aux mécanismes de la finance publique et aux réalités des marchés. Rationalisation des dépenses publiques, réforme des subventions, traitement de la dette, renforcement de la souveraineté économique et énergétique : le Premier ministre, Al Aminou Lo, qui présentait mardi, le fil conducteur de son gouvernement, devant la représentation nationale, n’a pas fait dans la langue de bois. Face aux députés, le chef du gouvernement a exposé, point par point, les principaux mécanismes sur lesquels son équipe entend s’appuyer pour donner corps à la vision du président de la République, Bassirou Diomaye Faye. « Le cap est maintenu », a-t-il d’emblée martelé, faisant ainsi référence aux orientations du programme qui a conduit le chef de l’État au pouvoir, porté par la confiance des électeurs. Actualité oblige, l’ancien secrétaire général du gouvernement, devenu Premier ministre, s’est également employé à clarifier la portée du programme conclu avec le Fonds monétaire international (FMI). Selon lui, les grandes orientations retenues s’inscrivent dans le prolongement des engagements antérieurs de l’État. Évoquant la nécessité pour le Sénégal de s’ouvrir davantage et de s’adapter aux réalités du moment, Al Aminou Lo a insisté sur une évidence : aucun État ne peut désormais vivre en autarcie. « Cette époque est révolue », a-t-il lancé en substance, rappelant que l’interdépendance des économies constitue désormais une donnée incontournable de la gouvernance publique. Le Premier ministre a également tenu à rassurer sur l’accompagnement du Sénégal par le FMI et les autres partenaires multilatéraux. Celui-ci, a-t-il soutenu, ne saurait remettre en cause la préservation des intérêts des populations, notamment ceux des couches les plus vulnérables. Le réalignement, dans cette perspective, ne devrait donc pas se traduire par un abandon de la protection sociale. Autre sujet sensible abordé devant les députés : la dégradation de la notation financière du Sénégal. Al Aminou Lo estime qu’elle traduit avant tout une certaine prudence des marchés, à l’égard de la situation financière nationale. Pour autant, le Premier ministre se veut rassurant : il n’y aurait pas péril en la demeure. L’heure est plutôt, selon lui, à la restauration progressive de la confiance. Une manière, pour Al Aminou Lo, de poser le débat sans fard : la contrainte financière est réelle, mais elle ne saurait, à ses yeux, remettre en cause le cap politique fixé par le chef de l’État. O.BA

items.title: Gnagna/Bogandé : Boubakar Konaté prend la tête de l’association FIIMBA
items.description: BURKINA-SIRBA-GNAGNA-GOUVERNANCE-PASSATION Gnagna/Bogandé : Boubakar Konaté prend la tête de l’association FIIMBA ‎ ‎Bogandé, 5 sept. 2026 (AIB)- L’Association FIIMBA a procédé, samedi à Bogandé, à la passation officielle de service entre ses coordonnateurs sortant et entrant, respectivement Hassane Guiré et Boubakar Konaté. C’était à l’occasion d’une cérémonie placée sous le signe de la continuité et du renforcement des actions en faveur du développement communautaire. ‎ ‎La rencontre, tenue dans la salle de réunion de l’Association FIIMBA, a réuni des représentants des autorités administratives, des services techniques, des structures partenaires, ainsi que des membres et sympathisants de l’organisation. ‎ ‎Elle a été ponctuée par plusieurs temps forts, notamment l’allocution de bienvenue du président de l’union, Tibandiba Ousmane Lankoandé, l’intervention du coordonnateur sortant qui a reçu une attestation de reconnaissance, la signature du procès-verbal de passation de service et la remise officielle des dossiers au nouveau coordonnateur. ‎ ‎Prenant la parole à cette occasion, l’ex premier responsable de l’association, Hassane Guiré a dressé le bilan de son passage à la tête de FIIMBA depuis sa création en 1996. Le nouveau retraité a notamment mis en exergue les principales réalisations enregistrées au cours de cette période, les expériences acquises et les défis relevés dans la conduite des activités. ‎ ‎Sous son impulsion, FIIMBA a développé et conduit plusieurs projets de développement, avec l’accompagnement d’une vingtaine de partenaires, aussi bien au niveau national qu’international. Le dynamisme insufflé à l’organisation lui a valu les félicitations de l’ensemble de ces partenaires, tandis que plusieurs actions mis en œuvre ont bénéficié de l’appréciation favorable des bailleurs. ‎ ‎Parmi les innovations portées par Hassane Guiré figure également la promotion du concept d’« animateur endogène », une approche visant à s’appuyer sur les compétences et les ressources humaines issues des communautés elles-mêmes pour accompagner durablement les actions de développement. Il est présenté comme l’un des premiers promoteurs de cette approche au sein de FIIMBA. ‎ ‎En signe de reconnaissance pour les services rendus, il a reçu une attestation et un cadeau symbolique pour son engagement, son leadership et sa contribution à la consolidation des acquis de FIIMBA. ‎ ‎Une dizaine d’autres attestations de reconnaissance ont également été remises à des membres et acteurs de l’association dont l’engagement et la contribution aux activités ont été particulièrement appréciés. ‎ ‎À l’issue de la signature du procès-verbal et de la remise des dossiers, Boubakar Konaté a officiellement pris les rênes de la coordination de FIIMBA. ‎ ‎Il a exprimé sa disponibilité à consolider les acquis et à inscrire son action dans une dynamique de continuité, de cohésion et de renforcement des interventions de l’association. Il a également appelé les membres, les partenaires et l’ensemble des acteurs impliqués à maintenir leur mobilisation autour des objectifs de FIIMBA. ‎ ‎La cérémonie de passation a ainsi constitué un moment à la fois institutionnel et symbolique, marquant le passage de témoin entre deux responsables. Elle a surtout été perçue comme une transmission de responsabilité, plutôt qu’une rupture, afin de garantir la continuité de l’œuvre collective engagée depuis la création de l’association. ‎ ‎À travers ce renouvellement à la tête de sa coordination, FIIMBA entend poursuivre son engagement en faveur du développement communautaire, en s’appuyant sur les acquis engrangés, l’expérience de ses membres, l’accompagnement de ses partenaires et la mobilisation des communautés. ‎Agence d’information du Burkina ‎AYT/ata/zs

items.title: New Ghanaian movie ‘Two’ to explore crime, faith and moral ambiguity
items.description: Two , a new Ghanaian neo-noir film, produced by Bravado!, LL Productions, Apstairs Media and WM Media, is in the offing. The film tells the story of a man who has retired and disavowed his life of crime after intentionally botching a task. Reformed and living a conservative life in a church, he falls in love and marries Elara, a girl in the church. As he settles into married life, his past comes calling when his mentor and boss comes back into his life. The appearance of Vic sets him on a path to tie up loose ends and leave his past for good. Two explores the themes of duality, good versus evil, perception versus reality, and moral ambiguity. Set in the bustling city of Accra and its surroundings, there is a high-octane hustle and experience of the city alongside church culture in a small Ghanaian church. The setting is candid, juxtaposing the light and dark parts of the city. It features actors Marcus Koranteng, Gideon Boakye, Elara Adjei, Dela Seade, Vic Togbor, Senanu Gbedawor, Inspector Obeng and Louis Lamis. According to the producers of Two , “This film is not a moral indictment; it is an invitation to empathy. We want viewers to sit with discomfort, to refuse quick condemnation. We want them to recognise a piece of themselves in the choices made on screen; to ask what they might do when the lights go out and the bills remain.” The production team comprises film stalwarts Nana Asihene, Louis Lamis, Aphua Larbi-Amoah, Isaac ‘Yaw Skyface’ Mensah and John ‘Kwame Black’ Markin. Nana Kofi Asihene, Director and Producer of the project, is an award-winning director, creative consultant and filmmaker. With over 150 music videos, short films and commercials shot, he has built a personal visual language that seeks to address the issues and spark inquest by using metaphoric relationships. His experience in crafting visual experiences through his background in music, photography, fashion and production design is invaluable to this project. ‘Two’ also has Louis Lamis as Writer. Louis Lamis is an award-winning director and producer with nearly two decades of experience creating compelling content that resonates deeply with audiences. He has directed and produced over 100 stage plays, more than 400 television episodes, and over 350 radio drama episodes, along with feature films, short films and documentaries. Renowned for his ability to craft stories that are both powerful and relatable, Louis brings this proven strength to make this project impactful and unforgettable. The next person is Aphua Larbi-Amoah, Producer. She works as a producer and writer and has worked on several local and international projects. She started as a production assistant and worked her way up to being a producer on different sets. Isaac ‘Yaw Skyface’ Mensah is also a Producer for the project. He is a cinematographer and filmmaker with over a decade of experience. After his graduation from Takoradi Technical University, he started his creative journey directing music videos for several top-notch artists. In the past five years, he has directed and produced several films to positive reviews. Lastly, there is John ‘Kwame Black’ Markin, Director of Photography. He embraces several viewpoints in creating meaningful artistic pieces through visual storytelling and loves to express the simple and complicated details of life through the visual medium. In the last three years, he has worked on various film projects such as The High Life , Nyame Mma , Paapa’s Life Lessons and Vagabonds . Check out https://www.thefilmtwo.com for more.

items.title: Indo-Ghana begins local liquid oxygen supply
items.description: Ghanaian hospitals, marking a shift in the country’s medical oxygen supply chain from cylinder-based distribution to a storage-based system designed to reduce shortages and improve reliability. The company delivered the first made-in-Ghana liquid oxygen supply to the Lekma Hospital, where a cryogenic storage system has been installed to receive, store and distribute the product through the facility’s oxygen network. Managing Director of Indo-Ghana Industries, Varun Tyagi, said the move addresses long-standing challenges associated with transporting medical oxygen in cylinders, including delays, high logistics costs and supply interruptions. “Over the years, one of the biggest challenges when it comes to distribution of oxygen is that the packaging material, the cylinders, are much more expensive than the product itself. In Africa, distribution costs are too high,” he said. Indo-Ghana, which began operations in Ghana in 2010, initially focused on the production and supply of gaseous oxygen. The company expanded into liquid oxygen production after identifying distribution constraints that became more visible during the COVID-19 pandemic, when demand for medical oxygen increased sharply. According to Mr. Tyagi, the cylinder-based model required hospitals to continuously request refills as empty cylinders were returned for replenishment, creating risks of delays caused by transportation challenges and road conditions. Liquid oxygen changes the supply model by increasing storage capacity. The company said a single storage tank can hold the equivalent of about 1,000 cylinders of gaseous oxygen, allowing hospitals to maintain larger reserves and reduce frequent deliveries. “At Lekma, the quantity of liquid that we supplied can sustain them for a period of at least three months. They can now be assured that for the next three months they have oxygen available in their facility,” Mr. Tyagi said. The transition has been supported by investments that have enabled hospitals to receive and store liquid oxygen. Mr. Tyagi said the initial challenge was not only producing liquid oxygen locally but ensuring healthcare facilities had the infrastructure to accept it. He said support from development partners, including USAID, CHAI and JHPEIGO has helped provide liquid oxygen storage tanks to about 10 hospitals, while another five facilities received similar support through other programmes, bringing the total number of hospitals equipped to receive liquid oxygen to about 15. Lekma’s Head of Clinical Engineering, Saviour Demordzie, said the new system has already improved oxygen availability at the facility by providing a more stable supply and reducing reliance on emergency cylinder deliveries. “Our frequent calls for oxygen have reduced. There is a constant pressure and flow of oxygen at the facility. And because it is a liquid oxygen plant, we have a higher purity of oxygen delivered to the patient,” he said. Before the installation of the liquid oxygen system, Mr. Demordzie said the hospital relied largely on oxygen cylinders, creating uncertainty when supplies ran low. “Initially, you had to call vendors when the oxygen was finishing, and if you were not fortunate, the unfortunate could happen,” he said. The hospital’s previous oxygen systems produced oxygen concentration levels of between 90 percent and 92 percent, while liquid oxygen provides oxygen purity closer to 99 percent, he said. Higher oxygen concentration is important in supporting patient treatment, particularly in critical care settings. Indo-Ghana’s Engineer, Eduardo Bojador Bonifacio, said the new system improves efficiency by reducing manual handling and allowing automated supply through pipelines connected to hospital wards. “This one can save time and minimise human error in supplying oxygen to patients,” he said. The company’s Apollonia Industrial Enclave facility has the capacity to produce liquid oxygen locally, with Indo-Ghana currently producing about 10 tonnes per day and planning additional capacity expansion. The company also produces other industrial gases, including nitrogen, argon, acetylene, ammonia and beverage gases. Mr. Tyagi said the company’s next phase is to develop a hub-and-spoke distribution model, where liquid oxygen production is concentrated at central facilities while smaller filling stations are established closer to hospitals across the country. “The idea is not just to limit it to one hospital. If there is a hospital in Yendi or any other part of Ghana, we want to supply through regional hubs so that the distance reduces and dependency reduces,” he said. However, the company identified several challenges that could affect the sustainability of medical oxygen supply. These include delayed payments from some hospitals, rising electricity costs and limited access to long-term financing. Mr. Tyagi said electricity accounts for about 42 percent to 45 percent of production costs, making power tariffs a major factor in the cost of medical oxygen. He also called for medical oxygen producers to be recognised as critical service providers, similar to arrangements in other countries where oxygen manufacturers receive priority support during power disruptions. “Medical oxygen production falls under critical industry. There should be provisions to ensure that if there is any power reduction or outage, companies producing oxygen are informed early and arrangements are made so that they are not disconnected,” he said. The company is also engaging with the Ministry of Health following the introduction of a national medical oxygen policy, which Mr. Tyagi said would support better monitoring of consumption, planning and supply management. He said the use of telemetry systems in newly installed tanks would allow hospitals and policymakers to track oxygen consumption patterns and prepare for periods of higher demand. “We are moving Ghana towards the next generation of medical services. Liquid oxygen is the first step towards making sure we are able to reach the last mile and make oxygen more accessible across the country,” Mr. Tyagi said.

items.title: Starlink: de milliers de villageois sénégalais risquent de perdre leur accès à internet
items.description: De milliers de Sénégalais vivant dans les zones reculées du pays risquent de perdre l’accès à internet si la suspension de la licence de Starlink, un service censé renforcer la connectivité dans les zones où la fibre n’est pas disponible, est décidée, alerte Senews.com, ce mercredi 9 septembre 2026. Avec la suspension provisoire de la licence accordée à Starlink, filiale de SpaceX spécialisée dans l’internet par satellite, par la Cour suprême du Sénégal, suite à une affaire judiciaire, la décision pourrait impacter négativement la vie de plusieurs dizaines de milliers de personnes vivant dans les zones rurales du pays. En effet, le déploiement de Starlink a été pensé pour soulager les populations des zones reculées dans lesquelles la fibre n’existe pas. Arrivé au Sénégal février dernier, Starlink était destiné a comblé le gap de la fracture numérique du pays. Selon des chiffres publiés en 2024 par l’Agence nationale de la statistique et de la démographie (ANSD) et l’Autorité de régulation des télécommunications et des postes (ARTP), l’accès à internet à domicile avait atteint «43,8% à Dakar» contre seulement «3% dans les zones rurales». Selon le média sénégalais, Starlink visait les régions orientales, notamment les localités de Tambacounda, Kédougou, les étendues du Ferlo à Matam, les villages insulaires et enclavés de la Casamance, de Kolda, du Walo et de Sédhiou. Par Wakat Séra L’article Starlink: de milliers de villageois sénégalais risquent de perdre leur accès à internet est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Alphabétisation au Mali : des centres à l’arrêt à cause de l’insécurité
items.description: Le monde a celebre ce mardi 8 septembre la Journee internationale de l'alphabetisation. Au Mali, elle constitue une veritable seconde chance pour ceux qui n'ont pas pu aller a l'ecole ou qui l'ont quittee trop tot. Mais l'acces a ces apprentissages restent fragiles dans certaines localites du pays a cause notamment de l'insecurite. Dispenses dans les langues nationales et adaptes aux realites locales, les cours d'alphabetisation permettent a de nombreuses personnes d'apprendre a lire, a ecrire et a compter. Ils contribuent aussi a ameliorer la gestion des activites economiques et les conditions de vie des beneficiaires. Dans plusieurs localites, des centres d'alphabetisation sont aujourd'hui fermes en raison de l'insecurite et du depart de certains partenaires. C'est le cas a Bankass ou les activites d'alphabetisation destinees aux femmes sont a l'arret depuis la crise securitaire. Le depart des partenaires a egalement affecte le fonctionnement des centres dans la zone. Une situation qui prive de nombreuses beneficiaires d'un apprentissage devenu essentiel dans leur quotidien. « Dans les centres d'alphabetisation, on nous apprend a lire et a ecrire. Nous apprenons a compter aussi. Cet apprentissage nous sert au quotidien et nous permet de mieux gerer nos activites economiques », temoigne Tessougue Lydie Ganna , formatrice au centre Alpha de Bankass. Selon elle, l'insecurite a entraîne le depart des partenaires qui soutenaient ces activites. Koulikoro face a d'autres difficultes a Koulikoro, l'alphabetisation se poursuit, mais les moyens restent limites. La commune urbaine compte cette annee 10 centres pour 179 auditeurs. Pour Souleymane Traore , chef de la section alphabetisation, plusieurs obstacles freinent encore le developpement de l'education non formelle. Les cours se deroulent parfois dans des conditions precaires. « Les cours sont dispenses dans des centres provisoires, sous les arbres ou sous les hangars », explique-t-il. « a cela s'ajoutent le faible engagement des collectivites, le manque de temps des femmes et les difficultes d'acces aux livrets d'apprentissage », poursuit Souleymane. Pour rappel, cette annee, la Journee internationale de l'alphabetisation est celebree sous le theme : « L'alphabetisation pour les peuples, la planete et la prosperite ». a travers ce theme, l'UNESCO met en avant les progres realises, mais aussi les priorites a definir face aux transformations d'un monde en pleine mutation. Lire aussi : L'alphabetisation des femmes deplacees, une voie vers l'autonomisation L’article Alphabétisation au Mali : des centres à l’arrêt à cause de l’insécurité est apparu en premier sur Studio Tamani - Informations, débats, magazines : toute l’actualité du Mali, en 5 langues .

items.title: El Ejército avisó el día 30 de una entrada “masiva” y “muy probable” cuando esta ya se estaba produciendo
items.description: El día 30 de julio a las 12.06 de la mañana, el Regimiento de Guerra Electrónica nº32 del Ejército de Tierra mandó a los servicios de inteligencia militares un mensaje clasificado donde advertía de una “entrada masiva” “MUY PROBABLE” aprovechando la festividad del Día del Trono en Marruecos. Una hora antes, sin embargo—y de acuerdo con el informe que la Policía Nacional entregó el 31 de agosto a la jueza de la Audiencia Nacional María Tardón—, el cruce masivo a Ceuta afrontaba su segunda oleada y ya se había producido “un desbordamiento del control policial debido a la presión acumulada”. A las 13.00, el Cifas (Centro de Inteligencia de las Fuerzas Armadas), destinatario del mensaje clasificado, emitía un documento sobre la situación en el que hablaba de “caos migratorio”, con las fuerzas españolas “desbordadas” ante la entrada de “miles de personas”. Tanto este como el primer mensaje del Regimiento de Guerra Electrónica han sido desclasificados este miércoles por el Gobierno . Seguir leyendo

items.title: PML-N, ANP senators spar over death of Gujranwala sanitary worker at Senate committee meeting
items.description: ISLAMABAD: A meeting of the Senate Functional Committee on Human Rights turned acrimonious on Wednesday as PML-N Senator Abid Sher Ali and ANP chief Senator Aimal Wali Khan clashed over the questioning of Suthra Punjab officials in connection with the death of a Gujranwala waste management worker. Chaired by Senator Samina Mumtaz Zehri, the committee was reviewing the death of an employee of the Gujranwala Waste Management Company (GWMC), who allegedly died by suicide after receiving half his salary and facing termination of his contract. Tensions rose when Senator Khan pressed officials with pointed questions. Senator Ali interrupted, objecting to the tone. “Listen to them — you are conducting an inquiry and asking questions as if you are sitting in a police station,” he said. When a member suggested that the cameras be switched off, Ali said he had “nothing wrong to say”. “Speak properly,” he told Khan. “I am speaking properly — you speak properly too,” Khan shot back. Senators, including Qurratulain Marri, intervened to defuse the situation. Officials told the committee that the worker had been with GWMC from 2024 to 2025 and that his contract had expired on May 31. The alleged suicide, they said, occurred after his employment had ended. Khan alleged that the worker had been paid only half his salary. “A common labourer was pushed to the point where he took his own life,” he said. The GWMC CEO disputed this, saying bank records showed full salary payments and that the worker had performance issues. Committee members questioned why Suthra Punjab was engaging a third party for cleaning staff instead of recruiting workers directly. Senator Marri pointed out that the Suthra Punjab Act came into force in 2026, while the incident took place in 2025. “How was recruitment done before the institution formally existed?” she asked. Khan echoed the concern. The CEO said the sanitary worker had initially been engaged in 2025 through a contractor and was later rehired and deputed to the IT room of the Suthra Punjab office as a naib qasid. He was later dismissed on grounds of misconduct, the committee was told. The GWMC CEO said compensation had been provided to the worker’s widow and children, including a plot purchased with the help of a chamber of commerce. When Senator Khan asked why a plot had been given if the worker was not in service, he remarked: “If you give me a plot too, I will also be happy.” Officials suggested the worker may have had personal problems. The ANP chief rejected the claim, saying: “You casually made an allegation that there was a love affair involved in why he died.” The committee directed Suthra Punjab to submit all relevant documents and copies of the laws for 2025 and 2026 and asked whether any redressal mechanism existed beyond financial compensation. The chairperson directed that the deceased’s family be invited to the next meeting to present their position. On July 1, a Suthra Punjab worker set himself on fire in Gujranwala in protest against non-payment of his full salary. He succumbed to his injuries two days later. A CCTV camera recorded footage of the employee when he was coming out of the office where he had gone to complain against the contractor, later showing him dowsing himself in petrol in the corridor in the presence of some staff members. Some other employees present there rushed to save their colleague and threw water on him, the CCTV footage showed. An official said the contractor had been illegally deducting a major chunk of the workers’ Rs21,000 monthly salary. On July 17, the Senate Functional Committee on Human Rights expressed concern over the worker’s alleged suicide. It sought complete records, including contracts, salary registers, tax documents and banking transactions, to examine possible violations. It also directed authorities to provide details of compensation and insurance for the deceased worker’s family. Other cases taken up The Additional IG Sindh briefed the committee on the case of Mir Raza. His father had reported him missing in July 2026. The first post-mortem was conducted on July 30, and a second was conducted at the request of the accused’s family. Senator Ali questioned the need for a second autopsy. The committee was told that the SHO had failed to preserve the crime scene and had shifted the body to the hospital. Both the SHO and DSP were suspended for negligence. The committee recommended the arrest of the SHO. On the Jaranwala incident of August 16, 2023, officials said 389 people had been arrested and several cases were under trial or had been concluded. Expressing concern over delays, the chairperson said the matter involved a minority community and required urgent resolution. Senator Ali stressed the need for justice and adequate compensation. The Chief Secretary’s representative said an assessment committee would evaluate losses with community representatives and that Rs2 million would be given to each affected family. The families, however, said the amount did not match their actual losses. The chairperson directed that compensation be determined on the basis of actual damages. The committee also reviewed the target killing of Ahmed Javed. It was told that the main accused, who was out on bail, was appearing in court with 40-50 people, allegedly intimidating witnesses. The committee recommended applying to the court to stop the practice. Senator Khan criticised the working of the CCD in Punjab and CTD in KP. items.title: Vo/Education : Des kits scolaires, des vivres et non vivres aux enfants à Vogan
items.description: Vogan, 9 sept. (ATOP) – Des enfants démunis et orphelins de Vogan, dans la commune Vo 1 ont bénéficié des kits scolaires, des vivres et non vivres le mardi 8 septembre dans la localité. Les kits scolaires sont composés des cahiers de 100 et 200 pages, d’ensemble géométrique, de règles, crayons, gommes, des stylos et de rouleaux de couverture kaki. Les vivres et non vivres sont constitués de riz, de maïs, de pâtes alimentaires et d’huile ainsi que l’accompagnement des frais liés à la scolarité des enfants au terme de chaque trimestre et de leur prise en charge gratuite au centre de santé de Vo-Koutimé en cas de maladie. Des boîtes de craies aussi sont allées aux directions des établissements fréquentés par ces enfants. Bello Osséni remet symboliquement un kit scolaire à un enfant Cette initiative qui est à sa 11 ème édition, est à l’actif de l’association « Eben Ezer Tout est Grâce ». Ce geste touche 115 élèves, 11 étudiants et 16 apprentis. Il leur permettra de bien étudier et mieux s’appliquer dans leur apprentissage durant l’année scolaire 2026-2027. Le préfet de Vo, Leguèdè Kokou Jérôme et le maire de la commune Vo 1, Dr Kalipé Kossi se sont réjouis de ce geste qui soutient les efforts du gouvernement en matière de l’éducation de qualité pour tous. Ils ont appelé les parents et tuteurs à surveiller les apprenants afin qu’ils ne deviennent pas des enfants déscolarisés ou abandonnés dans la rue. Le directeur exécutif de l’association, Bello Osséni a réitéré l’engagement de sa structure et de ses partenaires à « ne laisser aucun enfant sans espoir et contribuer autant que possible à lui offrir les meilleures perspectives pour son avenir ». Il a demandé aux enfants de respecter leurs parents, enseignants et encadreurs. ATOP/AKS/DHK/BV

items.title: Xiaomi dévoile le REDMI 17 : une batterie de 7 500 mAh, un écran spacieux de 6,9 pouces et une durabilité au quotidien
items.description: Ouagadougou, Burkina Faso, 9 septembre 2026 – Xiaomi a dévoilé aujourd'hui la série REDMI 17, la dernière génération de sa gamme de smartphones axée sur le rapport qualité-prix, conçue pour offrir une fiabilité toute la journée et un divertissement sans effort à un plus grand nombre d'utilisateurs dans le monde. Composée des modèles REDMI 17, cette série associe une batterie massive de 7 500 mAh (typ.) à un écran immersif de 6,9 pouces à taux de rafraîchissement élevé et à un système de double caméra IA de 50 MP, offrant une expérience smartphone durable et fiable, adaptée au rythme de la vie quotidienne. Batterie plus grande et charge plus rapide pour une fiabilité au quotidien La performance est au cœur du REDMI 17. Doté d'une imposante batterie de 7 500 mAh (typ.), le smartphone est conçu pour offrir une autonomie exceptionnelle et accompagner les utilisateurs tout au long de la journée. Qu'il s'agisse de streaming, de navigation, d'appels vidéo, de création de contenu ou de divertissement, cette batterie haute capacité permet de rester productif, connecté et de profiter de ses contenus plus longtemps, tout en réduisant la fréquence des recharges. Compatible avec la charge turbo 45 W³ et la recharge inversée filaire jusqu'à 22,5 W⁴, le REDMI 17 offre également une plus grande flexibilité au quotidien. Selon le type d'utilisation, il peut atteindre jusqu'à 28 heures de lecture vidéo, 91 heures d'écoute musicale, 46 heures d'appels ou 12 heures d'enregistrement vidéo, répondant ainsi aux besoins des utilisateurs les plus exigeants.² Un écran large pour une expérience visuelle immersive Le REDMI 17 est équipé d'un grand écran immersif de 6,9 pouces offrant une expérience visuelle idéale pour le streaming, les jeux, la navigation et la lecture. Son taux de rafraîchissement adaptatif pouvant atteindre 120 Hz ajuste intelligemment la fluidité de l'affichage afin d'offrir une navigation plus réactive tout en optimisant la consommation d'énergie.⁵ Associé aux certifications TÜV Rheinland Low Blue Light, Circadian Friendly et Flicker Free, ainsi qu'à la technologie DC Dimming, l'écran garantit un meilleur confort visuel, même lors d'une utilisation prolongée. Conçu pour accompagner les utilisateurs au quotidien, l'écran est protégé par le Corning® Gorilla® Glass 7i, offrant une meilleure résistance aux rayures et aux chocs. Avec sa certification IP64 contre la poussière et les éclaboussures ainsi que la technologie Wet Touch, le REDMI 17 assure une utilisation fiable et réactive dans différentes conditions d'utilisation.⁶ Design audacieux et novateur, à l’extérieur comme à l’intérieur Le REDMI 17 adopte un tout nouveau langage de design inspiré de la nature, décliné dans une palette de couleurs à la fois classiques et expressives, qui associe une esthétique épurée à une praticité pensée pour le quotidien. Disponible en Noir, Bleu Profond, Vert Chêne et Violet Lotus⁷, il offre un style moderne qui s'adapte à toutes les personnalités. Au-delà de ses nouveaux coloris, le REDMI 17 associe un écran plat, une architecture à cadre mat et un design Metal Deco pour offrir une apparence élégante inspirée des smartphones haut de gamme, tout en garantissant une prise en main confortable. Son écran à perforation centrale et ses bordures affinées renforcent l'immersion et apportent une esthétique plus épurée. Pour compléter cette expérience, le système Dynamic RGB Light personnalise les effets lumineux des appels entrants, des notifications, de l'état de charge, des sessions de jeu et de l'utilisation de l'appareil photo, ajoutant une touche de personnalisation au quotidien. Performances fluides pour le divertissement au quotidien Le REDMI 17 associe un matériel performant à Xiaomi HyperOS 3 afin d'offrir une expérience fluide et réactive pour les tâches quotidiennes, le divertissement et le multitâche.⁹ Équipé du MediaTek Helio G91-Ultra, il prend en charge jusqu'à 12 Go de RAM grâce à l'extension de mémoire⁸, permettant un lancement plus rapide des applications et une meilleure fluidité lors de l'utilisation simultanée de plusieurs applications. Xiaomi HyperOS 3 améliore encore l'expérience grâce à des animations plus fluides,⁹ une réactivité renforcée et des interactions plus intuitives au quotidien. Côté photographie, le système de double caméra IA de 50 MP capture des images nettes et naturelles dans les situations de tous les jours, tandis que la fonction Double Vue permet d'enregistrer simultanément avec les caméras avant et arrière pour capturer chaque instant sous plusieurs perspectives. Pour compléter l'expérience multimédia, les doubles haut-parleurs stéréo avec une amplification du volume pouvant atteindre 300 % offrent un son plus puissant et immersif pour les vidéos, la musique, les appels et bien plus encore.
